jobs.title: Chief of Staff
jobs.description:
About Shift5

Shift5 is building the data platform for onboard operational technology (OT). We deliver cybersecurity, predictive maintenance, and compliance capabilities that enable defense and commercial fleets to operate with greater readiness, resilience, and mission assurance.

We are seeking a strategic, financially minded Chief of Staff to partner directly with the CEO and help drive Shift5's growth, revenue performance, and operating strategy.

Reporting directly to the CEO, this role will sit at the intersection of executive leadership, Finance, Growth, and Revenue Operations. The Chief of Staff will help translate company strategy into measurable business outcomes, bring greater rigor to revenue forecasting and operating performance, and ensure the CEO and executive team have the data and insights needed to make informed decisions.

This role will also have significant ownership of Revenue Operations, including managing the RevOps function and a direct report supporting revenue operations. This person will be responsible for creating greater visibility, predictability, and accountability across Shift5's revenue engine.

This is not a traditional administrative Chief of Staff role. The ideal candidate is a highly analytical business operator who can move seamlessly between financial analysis, revenue strategy, executive decision-making, and cross-functional execution.

Note: This position requires U.S. citizenship due to federal contract requirements and access to controlled information.

What You'll Do

• Serve as a strategic and financial thought partner to the CEO, helping drive company priorities, revenue growth, and operating performance.

• Own and develop Shift5's Revenue Operations function, including management of the RevOps team.

• Drive rigor and visibility across pipeline, bookings, forecasting, conversion, revenue performance, and other key commercial metrics.

• Partner closely with the CEO, CFO, and Growth leadership on revenue planning, annual targets, forecasts, and compensation planning.

• Build and maintain dashboards and reporting that provide leadership with a clear view of pipeline health, revenue performance, and business trends.

• Analyze financial and commercial performance to identify risks, opportunities, and areas requiring executive action.

• Evaluate the ROI and financial impact of strategic investments, headcount, growth initiatives, and other company priorities.

• Establish operating rhythms around company KPIs and ensure leadership has clear accountability against business and revenue objectives.

• Partner across Finance, Growth, Product, Mission Delivery, and executive leadership to improve alignment across the revenue lifecycle.

• Prepare the CEO for board meetings, financial reviews, strategic planning sessions, and other critical company engagements.

• Translate complex financial, operational, and revenue data into clear recommendations and decision points.

• Lead high-priority strategic initiatives on behalf of the CEO and ensure decisions translate into clear ownership, execution, and measurable outcomes.

What Success Looks Like

• Become a trusted strategic and financial advisor to the CEO and executive leadership team.

• Establish a high-performing Revenue Operations function with clear ownership and accountability.

• Improve the accuracy and predictability of pipeline and revenue forecasting.

• Give leadership consistent, actionable visibility into the company's most important financial and commercial metrics.

• Create greater accountability around revenue targets, company KPIs, and strategic priorities.

• Improve alignment between Finance, Growth, and other teams involved in the revenue lifecycle.

• Identify revenue risks and opportunities earlier and translate those insights into action.

• Improve the CEO's ability to make fast, data-driven decisions and focus his time on the company's highest-impact priorities.

• Help Shift5 scale with greater financial discipline, revenue predictability, and operational rigor.

Compensation & Benefits

• Competitive base salary

• Bonus program and equity in a fast-growing startup

• Employer-paid medical, dental and vision coverage

• Health Savings Account with annual employer contributions

• Life Insurance

• Uncapped paid time off policy

• Flexible work & remote work policy

• Tax-deferred public transit benefits with Metro SmartBenefits (DC/MD/VA)

Equal Opportunity Employer

Shift5 is committed to equal employment opportunity and affirmative action. All qualified applicants will receive consideration without regard to race, color, religion, sex, sexual orientation, gender identity, national origin, disability, veteran status, or other protected characteristics.

The Material Handler plays a critical role in maintaining a safe, clean, and highly functional workplace environment, ensuring facilities operations and employee-facing services are delivered efficiently and professionally.

What Your Impact Will Be:

Facilities & Event Support

• Set up and break down event spaces, including tables, chairs, staging, equipment, and related materials.
• Support conference room and common area readiness to ensure professional presentation.

Day Porter & Campus Support

Material Handling

Abilities

Position-Related Duties and Key Responsibilities

jobs.description:
WHAT TO EXPECT 

Heron Power is a startup company building cutting-edge power electronics for the 21st-century grid. We aim to debottleneck the growth of electricity generation and consumption with scalable, innovative, and less costly hardware solutions, accelerating the electrification of everything.

Our first goal is to build better converters (inverters & rectifiers) to connect large-scale renewables, storage, and loads to the grid. Heron Power’s leadership team is made up of seasoned veterans who have designed and shipped gigawatts of power conversion products over the past decade.

We understand that no one individual knows everything. We will all learn a lot together and from each other. We strive to build a collaborative, enriching environment conducive to personal, technical, and career growth. You can expect to work in a dynamic and collaborative environment, driven by first principles engineering, solving difficult problems.




JOB OVERVIEW

As a Staff/Senior Staff Global Supply Manager, you’ll lead strategic sourcing for the critical components and assemblies that power Heron Link.  In this pivotal role, you’ll partner closely with the Head of Supply Chain and leaders across Finance, Design Engineering, NPI and Manufacturing to build a resilient supply base. You will ensure the commercial success of Heron’s supply chain, overseeing product cost and supplier performance. 




HOW YOU WILL CONTRIBUTE

 - Define and own the category strategies for key components and assemblies.

 - Achieve or exceed cost targets through data-driven should-cost modeling, market and commodity analysis, and disciplined negotiations.

 - Lead RFx processes and negotiate commercial agreements, including piece pricing, tooling/NRE, and key contractual terms.

 - Manage business risk through scenario assessment of capacity, geopolitics, logistics, and supplier technology / commercial roadmaps. Actively partner with the engineering team to identify/mitigate supply and demand challenges

 - Drive supplier readiness across prototype, pilot, and mass production builds to ensure smooth scale-up and launch execution.

 - Develop and execute the logistics and warehousing strategy associated with and in partnership with factory operations

 - Escalate key supply, cost, and/or quality issues with partner teams and collaboratively develop corrective action plans 




WHAT YOU WILL BRING

We’re open to early to mid-career candidates with or without leadership experience. Scope and responsibilities will scale with the right candidate.




MUST HAVE REQUIREMENTS 

 - 8+ years of experience in sourcing or procurement for high volume manufacturing

 - Degree in Supply Chain, Engineering, Business Administration, or equivalent experience

 - Deep category knowledge across mechanical, electrical (PCB/PCBA), and/or electro-mechanical components and assemblies

 - Strong negotiation and contract management skills

 - Experience leading cross-functional work-streams with engineering, operations, finance, legal and NPI teams to drive alignment and execute sourcing strategies

 - Excellent communication and interpersonal skills

 - Willingness to travel domestically and internationally often with short notice




NICE TO HAVES

 - Extensive supply chain or manufacturing operations experience with power semiconductors, electronic components, injection molding, stamping, sheet metal fabrication, printed circuit board fab and assembly and adhesives 

 - Prior supplier development supporting medium voltage (34.5kV) or grid-related power electronics, such as converters, switchgear, circuit breakers, dielectric materials, and bussing

 - Strong data analysis and visualization skills (Tableau, PowerBI etc.) 
   
   

If you are passionate about technology and enjoy working in a fast-paced environment, we would love to hear from you. Join us in accelerating the electrification of everything at Heron Power. 

Heron Power provides competitive compensation (salary and equity) and benefits.  The base salary range for the role is from $170,000 to $220,000.

jobs.title: Settlement Department Manager
jobs.description:
ABOUT THE ROLE

The Ward Law Group is looking for a Settlements Department Manager to lead the team responsible for valuing, negotiating, and resolving our pre-suit personal injury inventory. This is a true management role. You will not be assigned your own pipeline of files — you will be measured by the performance of the negotiators who report to you and by the results your department produces as a whole.

We are a structured firm. Our settlements function runs on documented workflows, defined stages, case-level data, and performance standards that are calibrated to how cases actually move — not on arbitrary monthly quotas applied uniformly regardless of treatment posture, policy limits, or jurisdiction. We invest in our infrastructure because we believe it is what allows a department to scale without burning out the people in it.

If you have spent your career being told to "settle more cases" without being given the systems, the data, or the authority to make that happen, this is the opposite of that environment. We are looking for someone who wants to build and run a department properly, with the tools and the support to do it.

WHAT YOU'LL OWN

Lead and develop the team

• Directly manage a large settlement negotiators and support team, including hiring, onboarding, training, and performance management.
• Manage through your people rather than around them. Your job is to raise the ceiling of every negotiator on the team, not to absorb the hardest files yourself.
• Conduct structured one-on-ones, file reviews, and coaching sessions on a consistent cadence, with documented follow-up.
• Build individual development plans that move each team member measurably forward on valuation accuracy, negotiation skill, and file velocity.
• Address performance and conduct issues early, directly, and in partnership with Human Resources — including documented corrective action when warranted.

Manage through metrics

• Own the department’s key performance indicators: settlement volume, average settlement value, policy-limits capture rate, net client recovery, time in each pre-suit stage, aged-file exposure, demand turnaround, and negotiator-level productivity.
• Set individual and team performance standards that account for jurisdiction, case type, treatment posture, coverage, and liability profile.
• Review pipeline and performance data weekly. Diagnose the cause when a number moves — process, staffing, training, intake quality, or medical management — and act on it.
• Report department performance, forecasts, and risks to firm leadership on a regular cadence, with analysis rather than raw numbers.
• Manage aged and stalled inventory deliberately so that files are resolved on their merits and not simply on their age.

Oversee valuation and negotiation

• Serve as the final internal authority on case valuation and settlement strategy within your approval limits, and escalate appropriately beyond them.
• Review and approve demand packages, settlement authority requests, and counteroffers for quality, accuracy, and strategy.
• Apply and teach sound valuation methodology across the full range of injury types and procedures — including soft tissue, injections, surgical intervention, and traumatic brain injury — and ensure the team is not undervaluing complex or high-exposure claims.
• Identify bad faith setups, policy-limits opportunities, UM/UIM exposure, and coverage issues early, and coordinate strategy with firm leadership.
• Personally handle or co-handle the department’s highest-exposure and most sensitive negotiations.

Own the process

• Maintain and improve the department’s standard operating procedures, checklists, templates, and case-stage definitions so that the work is repeatable and quality does not depend on who is holding the file.
• Partner with medical management on treatment monitoring, records and billing completeness, reductions, and lien resolution so files are demand-ready without unnecessary delay.
• Work closely with intake, case management, and litigation to ensure clean handoffs in both directions and to feed back what the department learns about case quality.
• Make sure every negotiated resolution is documented, compliant, and client-approved, and that disbursement is accurate and timely.
• Bring forward technology, reporting, and workflow improvements — and then implement them, measure them, and keep what works.

Protect the client relationship

• Set the standard for how clients are counseled through settlement: clear expectations, realistic valuation conversations, and no surprises at disbursement.
• Ensure the team communicates with clients in their preferred language, with the responsiveness and cultural fluency our client base expects.
• Resolve escalated client concerns personally and use them to identify where the process needs to change.

• Seven or more years of progressive experience in personal injury, with substantial time in pre-suit settlement and negotiation.
• Three or more years directly managing a settlements, pre-litigation, or case management team — not managing assistants, and not serving as a senior individual contributor with informal influence. You must have carried responsibility for other people’s results.
• Demonstrated experience managing through metrics. You have set performance standards, tracked them, held people accountable to them, coached underperformers, and made the call when someone was not going to get there.
• Command of case valuation. You can defend a number. You understand medical specials, treatment trajectory, procedure-level valuation, comparative fault, coverage layers, and how venue changes the analysis.
• Bilingual. Fluency in English and Spanish, written and spoken. This is essential to serving our clients and leading our team.
• Florida law. Working knowledge of Florida personal injury practice, including PIP, the statutory pre-suit framework, and applicable damages and fee rules.
• Systems and data fluency. Comfort working in a case management system and in reports and spreadsheets. You should be able to build or read a pipeline report and draw the right conclusion from it.
• On-site. This is an in-office role, Monday through Friday. Leading a department well requires being present with the team.

WHAT SETS A CANDIDATE APART

• Multi-jurisdictional experience —New York, Texas, or other high-volume personal injury states in addition to Florida.
• Experience on both the plaintiff and defense side, or exposure to litigation as well as pre-suit.
• A track record of building a department’s infrastructure — SOPs, scorecards, training programs, stage definitions — rather than inheriting one.
• Experience managing a department through meaningful growth in headcount or case volume.
• Deep medical management and lien negotiation experience, including letters of protection and health insurance and government liens.
• Formal management training, or a documented history of developing people who were later promoted.

WHAT SUCCESS LOOKS LIKE

First 30 days

• You know every file in the department’s inventory by stage, age, and exposure, and you know every person on your team — their strengths, their gaps, and their numbers.
• You have audited the existing workflow end to end and identified where files stall and why.

First 90 days

• Individual performance standards are in place for every negotiator, calibrated to their inventory rather than to a flat quota.
• A consistent cadence of one-on-ones, file reviews, and department reporting is running without prompting.
• Aged inventory has been triaged and has a documented resolution plan.

First year

• Department settlement value and velocity have improved measurably against baseline, without a decline in net client recovery.
• Valuation is consistent across the team — two negotiators looking at the same file arrive at substantially the same number.
• You have developed at least one team member into a senior or lead role.
• Turnover on your team is low and the people on it can articulate exactly what is expected of them.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

• Competitive salary commensurate with experience
• Professional development and continuing education support
• Collaborative, growth-oriented team environment
• Medical, dental & vision
• Hospital plans
• 401(k) Retirement Plan – Pre-tax and Roth post-tax contributions available
• Life Insurance (Company paid Basic Life and AD&D as well as voluntary Life & AD&D for the employee and dependents)
• Company paid short and long-term disability
• Health & Dependent Care Spending Accounts (HSA & DCFSA)
• Employee Assistance Program
• Tuition Assistance
• Paid time off and paid holidays

JOIN OUR TEAM

At The Ward Law Group, every role contributes to changing lives.

If you're looking for an opportunity to grow your litigation career, maximize client recoveries, and work alongside a high-performing legal team, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and become part of a team committed to excellence, accountability, and changing lives—one client at a time.

All resumes submitted by search firms to any employee at The Ward Law Group via-email, the Internet or in any form and/or method without a valid written Statement of Work in place for this position from The Ward Law Group HR/Recruitment will be deemed the sole property of The Ward Law Group. No fee will be paid in the event the candidate is hired by The Ward Law Group as a result of the referral or through other means.

At The Ward Law Group, we recognize our people are our strength. We are an equal opportunity (M/F/Disability/Veterans) and consider all applications without regard to race, gender, sexual orientation, gender identity, age, color, religion, national origin, veteran status, disability, genetic information or any other status protected by applicable law. jobs.title: Demands Manager | Personal Injury
jobs.description:
POSITION OVERVIEW

The Demands Manager owns the pipeline that turns a completed course of treatment into a complete, accurate, and timely demand package. You will manage the full sequence — ordering medical records and bills, assembling the package, ensuring the demand is written well, routing it for attorney approval, and confirming it goes out inside the required timeframe — across our Florida and New York matters.

This role is measured on deadlines. A demand that sits an extra three weeks costs the client leverage and costs the firm cycle time, and the department’s key performance indicators exist to make sure that does not happen. You will own those numbers, report on them, and manage the team to them.

To be clear about scope: this position does not carry settlement authority. Case valuation, negotiation, and the decision to accept or reject an offer remain with the assigned attorney. Your job is to make certain that when the attorney makes those decisions, the package in front of them is complete, accurate, and on time.

KEY RESPONSIBILITIES

Records and Bills

• Order and pursue records. Direct the ordering of medical records, itemized bills, and supporting documentation from every treating provider, facility, and imaging center on the file.
• Chase what is missing. Maintain an active follow-up cadence with providers and records vendors; escalate non-responsive providers rather than letting a file stall.
• Verify completeness. Confirm that records and billing are complete and reconciled before a file moves to drafting — no gaps in treatment, no missing ledgers, no unexplained balances.
• Manage authorizations. Ensure HIPAA-compliant authorizations are valid, current, and consistent with state records-release requirements (Fla. Stat. § 456.057; N.Y. Public Health Law § 18).

Demand Preparation and Writing

• Own package quality. Set and enforce the standard for what a demand package contains — liability documentation, medical narrative, itemized specials, wage loss, photographs, and supporting exhibits.
• Write and edit demands. Draft demands on the most significant files personally, and edit the team’s work so that every package leaving the department reads consistently and accurately.
• Maintain the templates. Build and keep current the demand templates, exhibit indexes, and checklists used across both offices.
• Reconcile the numbers. Verify that billed amounts, paid amounts, adjustments, and outstanding balances presented in the demand are accurate and tie to the underlying records.

Attorney Approval and Transmittal

• Route for approval. Submit every demand to the assigned attorney for review and obtain documented approval before transmittal. No demand leaves without it.
• Close the loop on edits. Incorporate attorney revisions promptly and track rework so recurring issues get fixed at the template or training level.
• Send on time. Transmit approved demands within the required timeframe, by the correct method, with proof of delivery documented in the file.
• Track response deadlines. Calendar and monitor carrier response deadlines and escalate to the attorney as they approach.

Deadline and KPI Ownership

• Own the metrics. Be accountable for the department’s KPIs on records turnaround, drafting time, approval cycle, and on-time transmittal.
• Report weekly. Produce aging and pipeline reporting for firm leadership; flag at-risk files before they become late files, not after.
• Manage capacity. Distribute workload across the team, identify bottlenecks, and adjust assignments to protect deadlines.
• Protect statutes and policy deadlines. Maintain the controls that ensure no demand misses a statute of limitations, notice deadline, or policy-required timeframe.

Team Leadership

• Supervise the team. Lead, train, and evaluate demand writers and records specialists across the Florida and New York pipelines.
• Train to the standard. Onboard new team members, run file reviews, and raise the writing quality of the group over time.
• Improve the process. Recommend and implement case management system, workflow, and vendor improvements that shorten cycle time.

REQUIRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Bilingual English/Spanish, spoken and written.
• Minimum of four (4) years of pre-litigation personal injury experience, including hands-on demand preparation and medical records management.
• At least one (1) year of experience supervising, training, or leading a team.
• Demonstrated ability to manage a high-volume pipeline against hard deadlines, with metrics to support it.
• Strong writing ability — demands that are organized, persuasive, and free of errors, requiring minimal attorney rework.
• Ability to read and reconcile medical records, itemized bills, and provider ledgers accurately.
• Experience at a high-volume plaintiff personal injury firm handling both Florida and New York matters.
• Working knowledge of pre-suit practice in at least one of the two markets, and willingness to learn the other:

Florida — PIP and the emergency medical condition determination under Fla. Stat. § 627.736, policy limits disclosure requests under § 627.4137, civil remedy notice practice under § 624.155, the good-faith obligations that apply to claimants when setting demand deadlines following HB 837, and letter of protection documentation under § 768.0427.

New York — No-Fault practice under 11 NYCRR Part 65, including NF-2 and NF-3 filing deadlines and denial timeframes, and coverage and SUM disclosure practice under Insurance Law § 3420.

• Proficiency with legal case management software, records retrieval platforms, and spreadsheets.
• Meticulous attention to detail and comfort being held to a calendar.

PREFERRED QUALIFICATIONS

• Experience building or rebuilding a demands workflow, including template and checklist design.
• Familiarity with records retrieval vendors and the economics of outsourcing versus in-house retrieval.
• Paralegal certificate or a bachelor’s degree.
• Experience reporting operational metrics to firm leadership.

COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

• Competitive salary commensurate with experience
• Professional development and continuing education support
• Collaborative, growth-oriented team environment
• Medical, dental & vision
• Hospital plans
• 401(k) Retirement Plan – Pre-tax and Roth post-tax contributions available
• Life Insurance (Company paid Basic Life and AD&D as well as voluntary Life & AD&D for the employee and dependents)
• Company paid short and long-term disability
• Health & Dependent Care Spending Accounts (HSA & DCFSA)
• Employee Assistance Program
• Tuition Assistance
• Paid time off and paid holidays

JOIN OUR TEAM

At The Ward Law Group, every role contributes to changing lives.

If you're looking for an opportunity to grow your litigation career, maximize client recoveries, and work alongside a high-performing legal team, we'd love to hear from you.

Apply today and become part of a team committed to excellence, accountability, and changing lives—one client at a time.

jobs.title: Logistics Specialist
jobs.description:
Schedule: Full Time

Job Type: On-site

Salary Type: Hourly

Req #: 3288

About the Role

Uber Freight is looking for a Logistics Specialist to join our Cross Dock Center of Excellence. This isn't just about moving freight; it’s about mastering the complexity of modern cross-dock logistics. You will be the architect of efficient transportation and facility flow strategies, leveraging cutting-edge technology to ensure high-stakes shipments maintain strict FIFO compliance, reach their destinations on time, and help mitigate impacts to the customer's budget.

If you thrive in a fast-paced environment where your decisions directly impact the bottom line, facility throughput, and the customer experience, this is the place to build your career.

Why Join Us?

• Technological Edge: Work with and integrate industry-leading Transportation Management Systems (TMS), Warehouse Management Systems (WMS), and data tools.

• Impact: You aren't just following a process; you’re analyzing freight flows, preventing bottlenecks, and recommending improvements that shape our cross-dock transportation strategy while minimizing downstream impacts.

What the Candidate Will Do

• Master the Cycle: Navigate the full lifecycle of an order—from inbound load building to outbound tendering—using our advanced TMS and collaborating seamlessly with WMS platforms to maximize peak facility potential.

• FIFO & Freight Flow Ownership: Take complete ownership of freight planning through the cross-dock facility, ensuring all inbound and outbound shipments are strictly planned and executed based on FIFO (First-In, First-Out) principles to maintain optimal throughput and avoid dwell times.

• Strategic Sourcing & Scheduling: Build powerhouse relationships with customer-selected carriers. Leverage pre-planned static routes and select the lowest-cost, most efficient providers from participating carriers, ensuring dock schedules align for continuous delivery.

• Data-Driven Problem Solving: Proactively identify performance trends, resolve shipment errors, and prevent dock bottlenecks. Ensure customer freight visibility by managing ASN/EDI data flows, as well as CSV shipment file uploads for non-EDI information.

• Act as an Advisor: Train new users on our systems (TMS/WMS interactions) and document standard operating procedures that set the gold standard for cross-dock operational excellence.

• Collaborative Resolution: Serve as the critical link between shippers, receivers, facility operators, and carriers to resolve complex transloading and logistical challenges with professional poise.

Basic Qualifications

• High school diploma or GED equivalent.

• 2+ years of relevant experience in transportation, logistics, or cross-dock operations (A Bachelor’s degree in Supply Chain or a related field may be considered in lieu of experience).

• Foundational working knowledge of Warehouse Management Systems (WMS) and inventory flow principles, including FIFO.

• Intermediate proficiency with Google Workspace or Microsoft Office Suite.

Preferred Qualifications

• Bachelor’s degree in Transportation, Logistics, or Supply Chain Management.

• 3+ years of deep experience in the logistics industry, with specific experience in a cross-dock or fast-paced transload facility.

• Proven ability to collaborate between TMS and WMS systems to drive operational alignment.

• Analytical Mindset: Familiarity with BI and Tableau reporting to turn data into actionable insights for facility and freight performance.

• Advanced proficiency with Google Workspace or Microsoft Office Suite.

Benefits & Compensation for U.S. Employees

Employees working more than 30 hours in the US at Uber Freight are eligible for benefits like a company sponsored health plan, dental and vision benefits, 401k match, financial and mental wellness benefits, parental leave, short- and long-term disability coverage, life insurance and more.  US based employees may also be eligible for a performance or sales incentive bonus program, participation in Uber Freight equity awards, and other types of compensation depending upon the role.

About Uber Freight

Uber Freight helps companies move goods more reliably and efficiently. We bring together the technology, people, and transportation capacity they need, using real‑time data from millions of shipments to guide smarter decisions. That helps customers spot issues early, avoid costly surprises, and deliver on time. Uber Freight works with 1 in 3 Fortune 500 shippers across North America and manages over $17B in freight. Learn more at www.uberfreight.com.

Candidate Privacy Notice

Uber Freight is committed to protecting the privacy of our candidates. We collect and process personal data in accordance with applicable data protection laws. For detailed information on how we handle candidate data, please review our Candidate Privacy Notice.

EEOC

Uber Freight is proud to be an Equal Opportunity/Affirmative Action employer. All qualified applicants will receive consideration for employment without regards to sex, gender identity, sexual orientation, race, color, religion, national origin, disability, protected Veteran status, age, or any other characteristic protected by law. jobs.title: Staff Software Systems Engineer
jobs.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.



Role Description

The Software Systems Assurance team at Form Energy is growing! We coordinate the software architecture, requirements, and verification strategy for Multi-Day Energy Storage products that enable gigawatt-scale battery power plants.

We are looking for a Staff Software Systems Engineer to act as the technical authority bridging complex software architecture, functional safety, and embedded hardware integration. Depending on your background, this role offers the opportunity to specialize in either Broad Systems Architecture (facilitating cross-team design of distributed, safety-critical systems) or Product Assurance & Formal Modeling (using MBSE/Requirements-As-Code to translate high-level security and safety specs into executable, version-controlled schemas and bare-metal execution).


What You'll Do:

 - Systems Decomposition: Distill, organize, and document the architectural structures, state machines, and requirements of a grid-scale battery electric storage system (BESS), from grid command down to battery cell firmware.

 - Cross-Functional Architecture: Facilitate the design and implementation of a distributed, fault-tolerant, safety-critical system, bridging the gap between controls, electronics, and power systems engineers.

 - Model-Based Systems Engineering (MBSE): Transition system state machines, Functional Safety (FuSA) Hardware-Software Interfaces (HSI), and Interface Control Documents (ICDs) from static documents into version-controlled data schemas.

 - Formal Authoring, Translation & Verification: Author/translate high-level security specifications and functional safety hazard models (UL 1998/5500, ISO 21434) into verifiable execution contracts and deterministic rules.

 - Disambiguation: Get in the code to get answers. You will locate and resolve ambiguity across the system, showing up for the team when context or clarity is needed.
   

What You'll Bring:

 - 8+ years of relevant experience in software engineering, embedded systems engineering, or product assurance, including 2+ years of technical leadership experience.

 - Demonstrated track record of delivering complex, production-grade embedded systems, safety-critical hardware/software, or service-oriented architectures at scale.

 - Fluency in architectural design, failure/risk analysis, and cross-functional communication (diagramming, explaining, and specifying on a near-real-time basis).

 - Strong foundation in discrete logic, mathematical modeling, or formal specification, with a demonstrated ability to implement executable specifications using structured data schemas (e.g., JSON Schema, Protobuf, YAML, CUE) rather than static documents.

 - Ability to collaborate across diverse, interdisciplinary stakeholders to achieve unified, highly robust hardware/software designs under tight deadlines.
   

Preferred Qualifications:

 - For the Assurance/Lab Track: Hands-on experience reading bare-metal C code and performing deep diagnostic debugging using protocol analyzers (Wireshark) and embedded debuggers across CAN, SPI, Ethernet, or Embedded Linux/MPUs.

 - For the Formal Modeling Track: Direct capability to decompose complex programmable component safety requirements (e.g., UL 1998, UL 5500) into concrete software safety assertions. Experience with formal specification tools (like TLA+) is a major plus.
   
   

#LI-Onsite



Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here. 



When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed.

jobs.title: Copy of Director, Brand Marketing
jobs.description:
Role Overview

The Director of Brand Marketing will be the steward and champion of the Alliance Animal Health brand, leading how AAH comes to life across audiences, channels, and experiences. This role owns the strategic vision, positioning, and activation of the brand and ensures it shows up consistently and compellingly for veterinarians, hospital teams, prospective partners, candidates, and industry influencers.

The Director will lead several of AAH’s most visible brand initiatives, including recruitment marketing, employer brand, and brand-forward events and experiences such as our signature VetTalks event. This role will also partner closely with Talent Acquisition, Business Development, Human Resources, Operations, and other teams to translate business priorities into meaningful brand strategies and programs.

As the brand function continues to grow, the Director will play a critical role in evolving AAH’s social media and PR strategy, shaping our presence across key channels, guiding thought leadership for executives and medical leaders, and helping position AAH as one of the most respected and talked-about brands in veterinary medicine.

This is a highly visible, strategic, and hands-on leadership role for a marketer who can set a clear vision, inspire a team, influence senior stakeholders, and ensure strong execution. The right person will be energized by the opportunity to build, experiment, and leave a clear, measurable mark on a growing organization.

Key Responsibilities

Brand Strategy & Leadership

• Own and evolve the strategic vision and positioning for the Alliance Animal Health corporate brand while providing leadership and governance across AAH’s broader brand portfolio.
• Translate the brand strategy into annual and multi-year roadmaps with clear priorities, initiatives, budgets, and success metrics.
• Serve as the internal voice of the brand, ensuring AAH has a cohesive, differentiated presence across channels, audiences, and experiences.
• Lead the development and ongoing evolution of brand guidelines, messaging frameworks, and toolkits for internal stakeholders and external partners.
• Advise senior leaders and cross-functional partners on how to bring the AAH brand to life through communications, campaigns, events, and other high-visibility initiatives.
• Lead, coach, and develop members of the Brand team, establishing clear priorities and creating opportunities for growth.
• Oversee agency, freelance, and vendor relationships within the brand function, ensuring resources are aligned with AAH’s highest-priority opportunities.

Recruitment Marketing & Employer Brand

• Partner closely with Talent Acquisition to develop and lead recruitment marketing strategies that drive candidate awareness, consideration, leads, and applications.
• Own employer-brand storytelling for AAH, bringing our culture, career opportunities, and employee experience to life in a compelling and differentiated way.
• Lead and execute recruitment marketing channel strategy across web, social media, job boards, email, events, and other emerging opportunities.
• Monitor recruitment marketing performance and continuously test and optimize messaging, creative, audience strategies, and channels.
• Develop and optimize candidate journeys and nurture programs in partnership with Talent Acquisition, from initial awareness through application, offer, and onboarding.
• Guide the development and versioning of recruitment marketing content and creative assets for different roles, audiences, and markets.
• Oversee employer reputation strategies across platforms such as Glassdoor and Indeed.
• Ensure recruitment marketing efforts are closely connected to broader AAH brand strategy while addressing the distinct needs of veterinary candidates.

Brand Portfolio Leadership

• Provide strategic oversight across AAH’s growing brand portfolio, including the Alliance Animal Health corporate brand and PriorityPet Urgent Care.
• Establish the overarching brand architecture, ensuring each brand has a clear role, differentiated positioning, and connection to AAH’s broader growth strategy.
• Guide and support the Brand Manager responsible for bringing the PriorityPet Urgent Care corporate brand to life, including its positioning, veterinarian recruitment strategy, corporate social presence, campaigns, and industry activations.
• Ensure the PPUC brand is consistent and scalable while maintaining a distinct identity designed to attract prospective doctor partners and support the growth of the de novo pipeline.
• Partner with Growth Marketing, Talent Acquisition, Strategy, Operations, and other leaders to align enterprise brand priorities with recruitment and business-growth goals.
• Establish shared standards, planning processes, and measurement frameworks across the brand portfolio.
• Maintain visibility into brand and recruitment marketing performance, helping the team translate insights into stronger positioning, campaigns, and channel strategies.
• Ensure clear coordination between enterprise-level brand building and the teams responsible for local hospital marketing, market launches, and grand openings.

Events, Experiences & VetTalks

• Lead the strategy, planning, and execution of brand-forward events, with an emphasis on:AAH’s signature VetTalks series, including concept development, programming, speaker strategy, promotion, attendee experience, and post-event content.Key industry conferences and trade shows where AAH shows up as an employer, partner, and thought leader.Select partner-, employee-, and candidate-focused events.
• Ensure every event reflects the AAH brand and creates a thoughtful, differentiated experience for attendees.
• Partner with cross-functional teams and external vendors on event branding, creative, programming, content, promotion, and logistics.
• Establish clear goals and measurement plans for major events, including awareness, engagement, candidate pipeline, partner relationships, and content value.
• Create repeatable playbooks and templates that allow events to scale efficiently while remaining consistent and on-brand.

Support for Business Development

• Collaborate with Business Development leadership to align brand strategy with partner hospital growth and JV acquisition goals.
• Develop compelling pitch materials, presentations, campaigns, and content that bring the AAH story and partnership model to life for prospective partners.
• Ensure brand consistency and impact across Business Development touchpoints, including conferences, dinners, webinars, email campaigns, presentations, and direct outreach.
• Support launch and integration plans for new partner hospitals from a brand and communications perspective.
• Identify opportunities to strengthen AAH’s reputation and visibility among practice owners and other priority industry audiences.

Brand Campaigns, Content & Communications

• Lead integrated brand campaigns that build awareness, consideration, and preference across priority audiences.
• Oversee the development of creative concepts, copy, and content across video, social media, web, email, presentations, and collateral for AAH.
• Bring “The Surprising Side of Corporate” and the broader AAH story to life through compelling, audience-centered storytelling.
• Shape AAH’s social media strategy and oversee the development of content that strengthens engagement, awareness, and reputation.
• Help evolve AAH’s PR and thought-leadership strategy, identifying opportunities to elevate executives, medical leaders, and the organization’s expertise.
• Manage creative agencies, freelancers, and production partners, ensuring high-quality work is delivered on time and within budget.
• Maintain and optimize AAH’s corporate website and key brand, recruitment, and Business Development landing pages.

Insights, Measurement & Brand Governance

• Define and track brand health and campaign performance metrics, including awareness, perception, engagement, candidate pipeline, partner interest, and business impact.
• Establish clear goals and reporting frameworks for major brand initiatives and investments.
• Regularly share insights, performance results, and recommendations with senior leadership and cross-functional partners.
• Use audience, competitive, and performance insights to guide brand strategy and identify opportunities for innovation.
• Manage the brand marketing budget, prioritizing investments based on organizational goals and expected impact.
• Uphold brand governance across the organization by reviewing high-visibility assets and coaching stakeholders on brand standards and best practices.

• Bachelor’s degree in Marketing, Communications, Business, or a related field; MBA or advanced degree is a plus.
• 8+ years of progressive experience in brand management, integrated marketing, employer branding, or a related discipline.
• Demonstrated experience owning brand strategy and translating it into integrated programs, campaigns, and experiences.
• Experience leading and developing team members and providing strategic direction across multiple areas of responsibility.
• Proven ability to influence senior leaders and align cross-functional stakeholders around a shared strategy.
• Experience partnering closely with Talent Acquisition on employer brand or recruitment marketing strategies.
• Experience developing or launching a new brand, sub-brand, location concept, or go-to-market platform is strongly preferred.
• Hands-on experience planning and executing events and experiential marketing; experience leading a flagship or signature event is a strong plus.
• Experience working with Business Development, growth, or other commercially focused teams is preferred.
• Strong experience managing agencies, production partners, budgets, and complex cross-functional initiatives.
• Experience with multi-stakeholder brands, including B2B, B2C, and talent or recruitment audiences, is preferred.
• Experience in healthcare, animal health, veterinary medicine, or another mission-driven service organization is a plus.
• Data-driven mindset with the ability to interpret performance metrics, communicate insights, and translate findings into action.

Skills & Competencies

• Strategic leader, practical doer: Can establish a clear brand vision, align others around it, and remain close enough to the work to ensure it comes to life effectively.
• Brand builder: Understands how to develop differentiated positioning and translate it consistently across audiences, channels, and experiences.
• People leader: Builds clarity, develops talent, and creates an environment in which team members can do their best work.
• Exceptional communicator: Strong written, verbal, and presentation skills, with the ability to tailor messaging for veterinarians, hospital teams, executives, candidates, and prospective partners.
• Influential relationship-builder: Develops trusted partnerships across Talent Acquisition, Business Development, Operations, and hospital leadership.
• Strong creative judgment: Recognizes compelling ideas and knows how to guide creative work so it is strategically sound, distinctive, and effective.
• Business-minded: Connects brand decisions and investments to organizational priorities and measurable outcomes.
• Skilled project leader: Brings structure to complex initiatives and can effectively manage multiple priorities, stakeholders, budgets, and deadlines.
• Creative and curious: Looks for fresh ways to bring the brand to life and help AAH stand out within veterinary medicine.
• Mission-aligned: Demonstrates genuine enthusiasm for supporting veterinary professionals and improving the lives of pets, pet owners, and hospital teams.

Compensation & Structure

• Competitive base salary (negotiable and commensurate with experience)
• Bonus opportunity targeted at 20% target bonus
• Additional growth opportunities as recruitment responsibilities expand
• Reports directly to ER/Specialty Talent Acquisition Manager

Join Us

If you love the ER/Specialty veterinary world, enjoy connecting with people, and want to help build something impactful, we’d love to talk with you.

WE ARE A DRUG-FREE, SMOKE-FREE, EQUAL OPPORTUNITY EMPLOYER.

Company Policy & Federal & State Laws Forbid Discrimination Because of Age, Color, Race, Religion, Sex, Disability, Sexual Orientation or National Origin

jobs.title: Mobile Phlebotomist (Everett, WA)
jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

At Sprinter Health, our mission is to reimagine how people access care by bringing high quality care directly into the home.

Using the same technology that powers leading marketplace platforms, we deliver care where people are, especially those who need it most.

We’ve supported millions of patients across 22 states and consistently maintained a 90+ NPS, reflecting the quality and experience we strive to deliver every day.

Our clinical teams are at the center of making healthcare more accessible, connected, and personal.



Where patient experience isn’t a metric. It’s a standard.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Sprinter, you’ll bring healthcare directly to patients in the comfort of their homes. You’ll spend your day on the road providing a variety of preventative and diagnostic services, including blood draws, vitals, height and weight assessments, urine collection, support with Annual Wellness Visits, and more.

This role is perfect for someone who enjoys independence, connecting with patients, and a workday that looks different from a traditional clinic setting.

What We Offer

 - Guaranteed daily hours

 - National Mileage reimbursement, currently $0.76/mile reimbursement starting at mile 31

 - Company paid healthcare premiums

 - 100% 401(k) contribution of 3%

 - Company provided equipment including iPhone, iPad, scrubs, and supplies


WHAT YOU’LL DO

Life as a Sprinter starts before the first patient visit. Your car becomes both your office and your lab on the go, so preparation and organization are everything.

 - Prepare for your day by reviewing your schedule and ensuring you have the proper supplies and PPE.

 - Travel to patients’ homes throughout your assigned service area.

 - Provide scheduled services including blood draws, vitals, height and weight measurements, urine collection, support with Annual Wellness Visits, and other preventative and diagnostic services.

 - Use your expert phlebotomy skills to make blood draws as comfortable as possible for each patient.

 - Create a warm, welcoming, and professional experience in every patient’s home.

 - Accurately document each patient visit using Sprinter technology.

 - Properly label, handle, and transport specimens for lab drop off or shipment.

 - Manage your time, supplies, and schedule independently as you move from patient to patient throughout the day.


SOUND LIKE YOU?


MASTER OF YOUR CRAFT

 - Do you have exceptional blood draw skills?

 - Have you been the “go to” for hard sticks?

 - Are you confident in drawing blood from a wide range of patients?

 - Are you comfortable learning and performing additional clinical services?


ROAD WARRIOR

 - Do you enjoy a change of scenery during your workday?

 - Are you comfortable spending a significant portion of your day on the road?

 - Are you willing to travel an hour or more to visit patients?

 - Can you comfortably drive before 7:00 a.m. when your first patient is scheduled at 7:00 a.m.?


PATIENT FOCUSED

 - Are you passionate about helping others?

 - Are you kind, empathetic, and an effective communicator?

 - Do you enjoy meeting new people and creating a great patient experience?


SEEN IT ALL BEFORE

 - Are you comfortable providing care in a variety of home environments, recognizing that each patient’s living conditions and standards may be different from your own?

 - Can you remain calm, adaptable, and professional when faced with challenging or unexpected situations?


COMMITTED TO EXCELLENCE

 - Do you pride yourself on being reliable, dependable, and trustworthy?

 - Are you solution oriented and able to think critically when challenges arise?

 - Is your mode of transportation as reliable as you are?


TECH PROFICIENT

 - Are you proficient using Apple iPhones and iPads beyond calling and texting?

 - Are you comfortable navigating apps, electronic health records, telehealth platforms, and other digital tools?

 - Can you confidently learn and navigate new technology independently?

If you’re nodding yes, you’re off to a great start. Here are a few more things you’ll need to be successful as a Sprinter.


WHAT YOU’LL NEED

 - Strong phlebotomy skills, including experience with challenging sticks

 - Patient facing healthcare experience as a Phlebotomist, Medical Assistant (MA), Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN), or Licensed Vocational Nurse (LVN) in home preferred

 - Current BLS certification

 - Valid driver’s license, current auto insurance, and personal, reliable vehicle

 - Availability Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m.–3:30 p.m.

 - Ability to drive before 7:00 a.m. to arrive at your first scheduled patient on time

 - Proficiency using Apple iPhones and iPads

 - Ability to meet applicable state specific certification or licensing requirements


PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

 - Ability to lift and carry up to 25 lbs.

 - Ability to spend prolonged periods driving between patient appointments

 - Ability to stand, walk, bend, reach, and carry medical supplies and equipment

 - Ability to safely navigate a variety of patient home environments, including locations with stairs

jobs.description:
Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company. We believe that data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are inextricably linked. Our mission is to enable the responsible advancement of artificial intelligence by providing the data, evaluation frameworks, and human expertise required to build AI systems that can be trusted at scale. We provide a range of transferable solutions, platforms, and services for Generative AI / AI builders and adopters. In every relationship, we honor our 36+ year legacy delivering the highest quality data and outstanding outcomes for our customers.

Scope of the Role:

We are looking for detail-oriented Voice Specialists to evaluate the performance of AI models through real-time, voice-based conversations. In this role, you will interact with two different AI models using the same assigned scenario, carefully compare their responses, and provide structured evaluations based on defined quality criteria.

The goal of the evaluation is to create a fair, consistent comparison between models and identify which model delivers the stronger overall conversational experience.

What You’ll Own:

• Review an assigned scenario and roleplay a natural conversation with two different AI models.

• Conduct comparable conversations with Model A and Model B, keeping the scenario, conversational approach, and overall interaction as consistent as possible.

• Maintain approximately the same number of conversational turns with each model to support a fair comparison.

• Record your voice during each interaction and pay close attention to the quality and behavior of the model's responses.

• Evaluate each model across five defined evaluation dimensions.

• Identify and categorize relevant error clusters that may occur in the audio or conversation.

• Compare the performance of Model A and Model B based on the evaluation criteria and your observations.

• Select the model that demonstrated the stronger overall performance according to the defined evaluation framework.

• Write a detailed rationale explaining your final preference, referencing specific examples and observations from both conversations.

• Apply evaluation guidelines consistently across different scenarios and model interactions

You’ll Thrive in This Role If You Have

• Bachelors Degree

• Strong attention to detail and ability to notice subtle differences in conversational quality.

• Excellent listening and comprehension skills.

• Strong written communication skills, particularly the ability to explain observations clearly and objectively.

• Ability to follow detailed evaluation guidelines consistently.

• Comfort speaking naturally and roleplaying different conversational scenarios.

• Ability to compare two interactions fairly without allowing personal preferences to influence the evaluation.

• Strong critical-thinking and analytical skills.

• Reliability and consistency when completing structured evaluation tasks.

• Familiarity with AI assistants, voice-based AI, or conversational systems

The expected hourly salary range for this position is $20-$27 p/hour, based on experience, skills, and qualifications.

Please be aware of recruitment scams involving individuals or organizations falsely claiming to represent employers. Innodata will never ask for payment, banking details, or sensitive personal information during the application process. To learn more on how to recognize job scams, please visit the Federal Trade Commission’s guide at https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams.

If you believe you’ve been targeted by a recruitment scam, please report it to Innodata at verifyjoboffer@innodata.com and consider reporting it to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.

The Field Access Manager (FAM) will act as the main point of contact at designated accounts providing account management support to Healthcare Professionals (HCPs) and their staff on behalf of patients who are prescribed a product for approved indications. The FAM will help coordinate pull-through efforts for patients who have been prescribed the product, irrespective of channel (HUB, specialty pharmacy, etc.), provided proper HIPAA consent has been secured from the patient. The FAM will be expected to be the primary face of the Patient Services platforms within designated HCP offices. The FAM is also responsible for partnering with internal and external stakeholders to optimize access to the product for patients.

jobs.description:
WHO WE ARE

At Sprinter Health, our mission is to reimagine how people access care by bringing high quality care directly into the home.

Using the same technology that powers leading marketplace platforms, we deliver care where people are, especially those who need it most.

We’ve supported millions of patients across 22 states and consistently maintained a 90+ NPS, reflecting the quality and experience we strive to deliver every day.

Our clinical teams are at the center of making healthcare more accessible, connected, and personal.

Where patient experience isn’t a metric. It’s a standard.




ABOUT THE ROLE

As a Travel Sprinter, you’ll take what you do best and bring it to Sprinter Health markets that need you most. One assignment may keep you closer to home, while another may have you packing your bags for an extended stay.

You’ll provide a variety of preventative and diagnostic services including blood draws, vitals, height and weight assessments, urine collection, support with Annual Wellness Visits, and more, while traveling to support different Sprinter Health markets.

This role is perfect for someone who enjoys independence, embraces change, and is excited by the opportunity to work in new cities and states. Travel Sprinters should expect to travel approximately 75% of the year and may spend extended periods away from home depending on their travel assignment.


WHAT WE OFFER

 - Guaranteed daily hours

 - Company provided lodging and transportation for travel assignments

 - Company paid healthcare premiums

 - 100% 401(k) Company contribution of 3%

 - Company provided equipment including iPhone, iPad, scrubs, and supplies


WHAT YOU’LL DO

Life as a Travel Sprinter can take you somewhere new, but the mission stays the same: arrive prepared, provide exceptional care, and create a great experience for every patient.

 - Prepare for your day by reviewing your schedule and ensuring you have the proper supplies and PPE.

 - Travel to patients’ homes throughout your assigned market.

 - Provide scheduled services including blood draws, vitals, height and weight measurements, urine collection, support with Annual Wellness Visits, and other preventative and diagnostic services.

 - Use your expert phlebotomy skills to make blood draws as comfortable as possible for each patient.

 - Create a warm, welcoming, and professional experience in every patient’s home.

 - Accurately document each patient visit using Sprinter technology.

 - Properly label, handle, and transport specimens for lab drop off or shipment.

 - Navigate unfamiliar cities, neighborhoods, and patient service areas independently.

 - Manage your time, supplies, and schedule as you move from patient to patient throughout the day.


SOUND LIKE YOU?


MASTER OF YOUR CRAFT

 - Do you have exceptional blood draw skills?

 - Have you been the “go to” for hard sticks?

 - Are you confident in drawing blood from a wide range of patients?

 - Are you comfortable learning and performing additional clinical services?


BUILT TO TRAVEL

 - Are you prepared to travel approximately 90% of the year?

 - Can you quickly adapt to new assignments and environments?


PATIENT FOCUSED

 - Are you passionate about helping others?

 - Are you kind, empathetic, and an effective communicator?

 - Do you enjoy meeting new people and creating a great patient experience?


SEEN IT ALL BEFORE

 - Are you comfortable providing care in a variety of home environments, recognizing that each patient’s living conditions and standards may be different from your own?

 - Are you comfortable navigating unfamiliar neighborhoods and communities?

 - Can you remain calm, adaptable, and professional when faced with challenging or unexpected situations?


COMMITTED TO EXCELLENCE

 - Do you pride yourself on being reliable, dependable, and trustworthy?

 - Are you solution oriented and able to think critically when challenges arise?

 - Can you remain flexible and adaptable while working away from home?


TECH PROFICIENT

 - Are you proficient using Apple iPhones and iPads beyond calling and texting?

 - Are you comfortable navigating apps, electronic health records, telehealth platforms, and other digital tools?

 - Can you confidently learn and navigate new technology independently?

If you’re nodding yes, you’re off to a great start. Here are a few more things you’ll need to be successful as a Travel Sprinter.


WHAT YOU’LL NEED

 - Strong phlebotomy skills, including experience with challenging sticks

 - Patient facing healthcare experience as a Phlebotomist, Medical Assistant (MA), Licensed Practical Nurse (LPN), or Licensed Vocational Nurse (LVN), with in home experience preferred

 - Current BLS certification

 - Valid driver’s license and auto insurance

 - Availability Monday–Friday, 7:00 a.m.–3:30 p.m.

 - Ability to drive before 7:00 a.m. to arrive at your first scheduled patient on time

 - Ability and willingness to travel approximately 75% of the year

 - Ability to be away from home for extended periods

 - Comfort driving and navigating independently in unfamiliar cities and neighborhoods

 - Proficiency using Apple iPhones and iPads

 - Ability to meet applicable state specific certification or licensing requirements


PHYSICAL REQUIREMENTS

 - Ability to lift and carry up to 25 lbs. as part of day to day responsibilities

 - Ability to perform heavier lifting when required for travel assignments

 - Ability to spend prolonged periods driving between patient appointments

 - Ability to stand, walk, bend, reach, and carry medical supplies and equipment

 - Ability to safely navigate a variety of patient home environments, including locations with stairs

 - Ability to manage the physical demands associated with frequent travel

jobs.title: Senior Staff Quantum Scientist
jobs.location: Albuquerque, New Mexico, United States; Boulder, Colorado, United States
jobs.description:
About IonQ:

IonQ, Inc. [NYSE: IONQ] is the world’s leading quantum platform and merchant supplier - delivering integrated quantum solutions across computing, networking, sensing, and security. IonQ’s newest generation of quantum computers, the IonQ Tempo, is the latest in a line of cutting-edge systems that have been helping customers and partners including Amazon Web Services, and AstraZeneca achieve 20x performance results and accelerate innovation in drug discovery, materials science, financial modeling, logistics, cybersecurity, and defense. In 2025, the company achieved 99.99% two-qubit gate fidelity, setting a world record in quantum computing performance.

Headquartered in College Park, Maryland, IonQ has operations in California, Colorado, Massachusetts, Tennessee, Washington, Italy, South Korea, Sweden, Switzerland, Canada, and the United Kingdom. Our quantum computing services are available through all major cloud providers, while we also meet the needs of networking and sensing customers across land, sea, air, and space. IonQ is making quantum platforms more accessible and impactful than ever before.

Role Overview

Role:

We are looking for a Senior Staff Quantum Scientist to join our Science team at IonQ. In this role, you will take a leading role in our research efforts, driving experimental efforts and the architecture of our future generation quantum systems.

We are pioneering advancements in quantum computing by utilising trapped ion technology and our proprietary laser-free quantum control methods. Our research and development efforts build on our fully integrated quantum processors that can be fabricated within standard silicon foundries. This unique approach allows us to leverage the highest-performing qubit technology while ensuring scalability and manufacturability using existing semiconductor fabrication technology.

We approach quantum computing with a focus on minimising errors, striving to achieve ultra-low gate errors at scale. Our immediate objective is to develop functional quantum computers within the NISQ regime, aiming to construct fault-tolerant machines that require minimal QEC overhead. Our recent breakthroughs include achieving 99.97% fidelity in two-qubit gates and 99.9992% fidelity in single-qubit operations without error correction, setting new industry standards for performance.

Responsibilities:

As a Senior Staff Quantum Scientist you will be at the forefront of our research and development, taking a leading role within our experimental science team. You will be responsible for driving innovation in coherent control, calibration, and benchmarking at scale, with a particular focus on enabling ultra-low error rates and system reliability across larger trapped-ion devices.

You will work hands-on with our current hardware, with work spanning design, debugging, and executing experiments, developing novel control schemes, and pushing the boundaries of system performance.

Beyond hands-on experiments, you will help shape technical direction, mentor junior scientists, and ensure our work translates into scalable, fault-tolerant systems.

Key responsibilities include:

• Lead the prototyping and characterisation of advanced coherent control schemes for trapped-ion qubits using laser and microwave fields.

• Drive system-level benchmarking and optimisation, ensuring near-term devices achieve world-leading performance and stability.

• Validate and integrate new trap technologies (e.g. on-chip electronics or photonics) to support scaling towards error-corrected architectures.

• Guide junior scientists in experimental design, analysis, and presentation of results.

• Represent IonQ at conferences and external collaborations.

Requirements:

To be successful, you will need a strong foundation in atomic or qubit-related physics, developed through a PhD in physics or a closely related discipline, or an equivalent combination of education and practical experience. We are looking for at least seven years of post-PhD experience in academia or industry, or equivalent relevant research experience, with the ability to lead projects, work autonomously and guide junior scientists.

Proven experience in quantum control, with hands-on work in calibration, benchmarking or coherent control of qubits, will be key to success. Practical skills in control software, hardware integration or experimental data analysis are also important.

You’d be a great fit with:

This work connects experimental physics with control hardware, software and data analysis. Experience linking these areas will help you investigate system performance and develop coherent control schemes for trapped-ion devices.

Technical leadership also means helping colleagues design experiments and communicate their results. Your experience of collaboration, mentoring and sharing scientific findings will support that part of the role.

• Deep experience in AMO physics or quantum computing. Trapped-ion experience is useful but is not required.

• Experience in spectroscopy or simulation of multilevel systems, control hardware characterisation, gate fidelity benchmarking or running algorithms on hardware.

• Strong proficiency in programming and data analysis.

• A track record of collaboration across teams and clear communication of complex scientific results through publications, talks or conferences.

The total compensation package includes base salary, bonus, equity, and a range of benefits available on our career site.

Compensation will vary based on individual factors such as education, qualifications, and experience of the final candidate(s), specific office location, and calibration against relevant market data and internal team equity. Posted base salary figures are subject to change as new market data becomes available. Our benefits include comprehensive medical, dental, and vision plans, matching 401(k), unlimited PTO and paid holidays, parental/adoption leave, legal insurance, and a home technology stipend. Details of participation in these benefit plans will be provided when a candidate receives an offer of employment.

At IonQ, we believe in fair treatment, access, opportunity, and advancement for all while striving to identify and eliminate barriers. We empower employees to thrive by fostering a culture of autonomy, productivity, and respect. We are dedicated to creating an environment where individuals can feel welcomed, respected, supported, and valued.

SpaceX was founded under the belief that a future where humanity is out exploring the stars is fundamentally more exciting than one where we are not. Today SpaceX is actively developing the technologies to make this possible, with the ultimate goal of enabling human life on Mars.

ELECTRICAL ENGINEER, BATTERY (FALCON & DRAGON)

As an Electrical Battery Engineer on the Falcon & Dragon Avionics Hardware Development team, you will have the unique opportunity to explore all areas of a battery’s life cycle from development through production and launch by engaging in multiple disciplines with a focus on design, reliability, and manufacturing. In addition to designing new assemblies from scratch, you will be expected to analyze and troubleshoot electronic/pack assemblies, define and optimize new processes, design circuits/fixtures/tools, and identify opportunities for improvement in both products and processes. • Drive changes to electrical schematics and mechanical drawings that improve reliability and manufacturability

jobs.title: AI Agentic Workflow Reviewer
jobs.description:
Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company. We believe that data and Artificial Intelligence (AI) are inextricably linked. Our mission is to enable the responsible advancement of artificial intelligence by providing the data, evaluation frameworks, and human expertise required to build AI systems that can be trusted at scale. We provide a range of transferable solutions, platforms, and services for Generative AI / AI builders and adopters. In every relationship, we honor our 36+ year legacy delivering the highest quality data and outstanding outcomes for our customers.

Scope of the Role:

We're building a dedicated reviewer team to evaluate complex, real-world agentic AI workflows, assessing whether AI agents complete tasks safely, respect user intent and consent, and hold up under close scrutiny. This isn't routine content moderation: reviewers work through ambiguous, multi-step scenarios where judgment calls matter as much as checklists. You'll operate inside isolated test environments, apply structured rubrics, and help calibrate what "safe and policy adherent agent behavior" actually looks like.

What You’ll Own:

• Review multi-step agent task trajectories against rubric-based criteria covering task success, safety, and policy adherence

• Evaluate whether an agent respected user agency and informed consent — not just whether it followed literal instructions

• Apply privacy guardrails when reviewing tasks involving sensitive or personal data

• Work inside isolated test environments, including verifying environment resets between test runs to prevent cross-contamination

• Flag and escalate safety-relevant or ambiguous findings through defined escalation paths

You’ll Thrive in This Role If You Have:

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

• 2–5+ years in quality review, QA/QC, trust & safety, content moderation, data annotation, or a similarly judgment-intensive review role

• Strong written communication – you can justify a scoring decision clearly enough for someone else to audit it

• Comfort with ambiguity and structured decision-making under a rubric, rather than needing a fixed rulebook for every case

• Baseline understanding of AI/ML concepts and how AI agents complete tasks (can be learned through onboarding, but some familiarity helps)

The expected hourly salary range for this position is $50-$55p/hour, based on experience, skills, and qualifications.

Please be aware of recruitment scams involving individuals or organizations falsely claiming to represent employers. Innodata will never ask for payment, banking details, or sensitive personal information during the application process. To learn more on how to recognize job scams, please visit the Federal Trade Commission’s guide at https://consumer.ftc.gov/articles/job-scams.

If you believe you’ve been targeted by a recruitment scam, please report it to Innodata at verifyjoboffer@innodata.com and consider reporting it to the FTC at ReportFraud.ftc.gov.
