jobs.title: Member of Technical Staff, Beneficial Deployments
jobs.description:
OpenEvidence is the most widely used medical AI platform in the world.

In just over a year, our usage has grown to >40% of US clinicians via product-led word of mouth adoption. We are a $12B company with a 30 person engineering team from MIT, Harvard, and Stanford. We believe world-changing products come from a small group of exceptional, autonomous builders, organized along focused objectives and empowered to take individual ownership and run fast. We are growing our team to seize a once-in-a-lifetime opportunity to define the default platform for medical AI. If you are a world-class engineer or scientist looking to define the bleeding edge and deliver concrete outcomes that impact hundreds of millions of lives, we want to talk.



Culture

We believe work is something that should be engaged with at a world-class level. Building 0->1  and scaling 1->1000 are professional sports, and uncompromising excellence is the bar. We believe building technologies that haven't existed is only possible with end to end ownership. We don't have separate product managers–every engineer and scientist is responsible for landing major improvements to the product. Important things are accomplished when an individual decides to accomplish them.



We believe that work should be hard. We believe good work is precise and intentional. Doing something a certain way just because that's how others are doing it guarantees mediocrity. We believe the quality of the product is paramount and the smallest details matter most. At the same time, developer and product velocity are essential. The best engineers know how to jump right to the hardest part of the problem and take every possible shortcut while keeping the user experience pristine. We believe an engineer's job is to complete and announce important projects and demonstrate their impact, or fail fast and pivot.



Who are you?

If you are looking to complete tickets 9-5 that someone else assigns, this job is not for you. If you are looking to write papers, this job is not for you. If you are looking to lean in and get your hands dirty, bruised, and bloody making something from nothing, personally impact hundreds of millions of lives, and drive ten figures of revenue, this job might be for you.



The ideal candidate is a brilliant builder. They are smart, ambitious, scrappy, autonomous, precise, motivated, hard-working, and low-ego. Does that sound rare? It is rare, we have only found 30 of them, and we would like to find more.




Skillsets

Specific skillsets are secondary, but some important spikes for different facets of our work are:



Fullstack

 - You love building end-to-end and seeing ideas through to completion.

 - The concept of creating something with your own two hands and then seeing that used and loved by millions of the most discerning users in the world is highly motivating.

Frontend and/or mobile

 - You are personally in control of the direct user experience. You have extreme attention to detail, and strive to make beautiful, modern, intentional interfaces.

 - You might have experience building beautiful mobile apps that users find to be a joy to use.

Machine learning

 - You have experience pushing the boundaries of what modern models are capable of.

 - You have a background in research, but find yourself drawn to actually making things instead of writing papers, and want real ownership and autonomy to build the future.

 - Evaluation and quantitative proof are first-class citizens to you.

Infrastructure / site reliability

 - Every single moment of downtime for a service used in literally life or death moments is something you want to personally eliminate.

 - You thrive building robust, optimized backends for mission-critical domains.

Speed

 - You know that improving speed doesn’t just make things faster, it can completely transform the user experience.

 - You enjoy tracking down and optimizing away every single source of inefficiency to create magical experiences for users.

Applied AI

 - You excel at building end-to-end systems grounded in a strong intuition about how to leverage modern models as components of extremely thoughtful, intentional systems.



Our engineering team is in-person 5 days a week in SF and Miami. We believe in creating an environment that optimizes for focus and productivity, including providing meals, transport and anything else you need to move quickly.

jobs.title: Clinical Lead, Beneficial Deployments
jobs.description:
OpenEvidence is the most widely used medical AI platform in the world.

In just over a year, our usage has grown to >65% of US clinicians via product-led word of mouth adoption. We are a $12B company with a 30 person engineering team from MIT, Harvard, and Stanford. We believe world-changing products come from a small group of exceptional, autonomous builders, organized along focused objectives and empowered to take individual ownership and run fast. We are now bringing OpenEvidence to clinicians and health workers in low- and middle-income countries, where access to high-quality medical expertise is scarcest and the stakes are highest. Doing that responsibly means proving, to a credible standard, that it is accurate, safe, and useful at the point of care in those settings. If you are a world-class clinician-scientist who wants to own that proof and shape how the best medical AI in the world is validated and adapted for the places that need it most, we want to talk.



Culture

We believe work is something that should be engaged with at a world-class level. Building 0->1 and scaling 1->1000 are professional sports, and uncompromising excellence is the bar. We believe building things that haven't existed is only possible with end to end ownership. We don't have separate project managers or study coordinators; you are responsible for defining what we need to prove, to what standard, and with whom, and for driving it to a result. Important things are accomplished when an individual decides to accomplish them.

We believe that work should be hard. We believe good work is precise and intentional. Doing something a certain way just because that's how others in digital health are doing it guarantees mediocrity. We believe the quality of the product is paramount and the smallest details matter most, and nowhere more than in the gap between benchmark performance and real-world clinical safety. At the same time, velocity is essential. The best clinician-scientists know how to jump right to the hardest part of the problem and focus on patient safety. We believe your job is to complete and announce important evaluations and demonstrate their impact.



Who are you?

If you are looking to run studies someone else designed, this job is not for you. If you are looking to write papers as an end in itself, this job is not for you. If you are looking to lean in and get your hands dirty, bruised, and bloody building the clinical evidence base for medical AI in low-resource settings from nothing, shaping the safeguards at the point of care, and impacting hundreds of millions of lives, this job might be for you.

The ideal candidate is a brilliant builder who is also a practicing clinician. They are smart, ambitious, scrappy, autonomous, precise, motivated, hard-working, and low-ego. They have medical training and clinical practice (MD, GP, MBBS, or equivalent) with direct experience delivering care, and they reason fluidly from how diagnosis, triage, treatment, and referral actually happen at the bedside. They have a concrete, on-the-ground understanding of clinical and care-delivery workflows in LMICs and what those workflows mean for how AI tools must be designed and evaluated. Does that sound rare? It is rare, and we would like to find them.



The role

You will own the clinical research and evaluation agenda for OpenEvidence in global health. You will design the clinical evaluations and validation frameworks that establish how OpenEvidence performs in LMIC contexts, covering accuracy, safety, multilingual performance, and real-world conditions, working side by side with our research, evaluation, and product teams. You will develop theories of change and outcome metrics that connect OpenEvidence's capabilities to care quality, health-worker performance, and patient outcomes, and you will help shape the safeguards that make the product safe and usable at the point of care. You will stay grounded in how care is actually delivered in low-resource settings and translate that into product improvements, not just evaluations. You will join a small, tight-knit global health team: you lead on this domain, but you should expect to roll up your sleeves on adjacent workstreams, help set overall strategy, and be a thought partner to colleagues working on other parts of the health system. You will spend roughly 25% of your time at research and partner sites.



Skillsets

Specific skillsets are secondary to the clinician-builder profile above, but some important spikes for different facets of this work are:



Clinical AI evaluation

 - You have direct experience evaluating or validating clinical AI/ML tools, and you understand the gap between benchmark performance and real-world clinical safety.

 - You have deep expertise in clinical research and evidence generation for digital health or AI tools, with a clear view of what counts as credible evidence for safety and effectiveness. Evaluation and quantitative proof are first-class citizens to you.

Regulatory and normative landscape

 - You have a strong command of the regulatory and normative landscape for clinical AI, including WHO processes, national regulatory authorities in LMICs, and research ethics.

Research partnerships

 - You have a track record of building research partnerships with academic and in-country researchers, and you treat local partners as scientific collaborators rather than data-collection sites.

 - You may have worked with philanthropic funders on evidence generation or research strategy.

Industry and field experience

 - You might have experience at a healthtech or AI company in clinical validation, clinical quality, or medical affairs, or a publication record in digital health, clinical AI evaluation, or implementation science.

 - You might have direct clinical experience in a low- or middle-income country, including with humanitarian or global-health delivery organizations.



We work in person in Miami and SF, and this role travels regularly (~25%) to research and partner sites. We believe in creating an environment that optimizes for focus and productivity, including providing meals, transport, and anything else you need to move quickly.

jobs.title: Quality Lead, Agentic AI Workflow Evaluation

Innodata (Nasdaq: INOD) is a global data engineering company. We are standing up a dedicated onsite team to evaluate complex, real-world agentic AI workflows for a frontier AI customer. Reviewers work through ambiguous, multi-step scenarios inside isolated test environments, assessing whether AI agents complete tasks safely, respect user intent and consent, and hold up under close scrutiny. The Quality Lead is the person accountable for whether that output is any good.

This is a senior individual contributor role. You will not manage the reviewers — that sits with the Engagement Manager — but you set the standard they are held to. You own the audit sample, run calibration, keep the rubric usable as real cases stress it, and train reviewers into the work. You are also the deputy: when the Engagement Manager is out, the engagement runs on you.

The quality approach here is not fully defined. We expect you to build it in partnership with the customer's quality leads, or at minimum to take what they have, run it honestly, and come back with specific recommendations for where it falls short.

What You’ll Own:

• Own the quality system for the engagement: audit design, sampling strategy, scoring standards, and how quality gets measured and reported

• Build that system with the customer's quality leads where none exists, and where one does, operate it and recommend concrete improvements based on what the data shows

• Re-score a sample of reviewer output as a second pass; identify error patterns rather than isolated mistakes

• Run calibration sessions: surface disagreement, work it to resolution, and document the reasoning so the outcome holds for future cases

• Maintain rubric health — flag criteria that are ambiguous, overlapping, or silent on cases the team keeps hitting, and drive revisions through the customer

• Train and onboard new reviewers, including nesting plans, ramp criteria, and the judgment call on when someone is production-ready

• Give the Engagement Manager the evidence behind performance conversations: who is drifting, on what, and whether coaching is working

• Report quality trends to the Engagement Manager and, alongside them, to the customer

• Deputize for the Engagement Manager on delivery operations during absences

• Maintain information security, privacy, and facility access practices required by the customer's onsite environment

You’ll Thrive in This Role If You Have:

• Bachelor's degree or equivalent practical experience

• 4+ years in quality assurance, quality management, or senior review work within annotation, evaluation, trust and safety, or a similarly judgment-intensive domain

• Direct experience owning a quality function: you designed the audit, not just executed someone else’s

• Significant experience with AI/ML evaluation work: annotation, red-teaming, RLHF, model or agent evaluation, or trust and safety review

• Hands-on familiarity with agentic systems: tool use, multi-step task execution, sandboxed environments, and common failure modes

• Demonstrated ability to run calibration with peers — including holding a position under disagreement and changing it when the argument is better

• Strong written communication; able to document a scoring standard clearly enough that a reviewer can apply it and an auditor can check it

• Comfortable in spreadsheets and in a dashboarding tool, with enough Python or SQL to pull and slice your own data (you will not be asked to build interfaces)

• Experience training or onboarding reviewers into rubric-based work

jobs.title: Sr Director, Operations and Supply Chain
jobs.description:
About Us

Connected International, Inc. (Connected Cannabis Co.) is a leading vertically integrated cannabis company based in Sacramento and operating in California, Arizona, and Florida. With over 11 years experience, Connected specializes in breeding, growing, manufacturing, and distributing top-shelf cannabis through its state-of-the-art facilities and proprietary genetics.

With over 250 employees across the United States, Connected maintains a strong presence in the industry across multiple markets. The company has recently expanded into Arizona and Florida with ambitious national expansion plans underway. Connected's mission has always been to breed, grow, and sell the best cannabis in the world, setting high standards for its products, people, and partners wherever we go.

About the Job

The Sr Director, Operations is responsible for leading and optimizing the end-to-end California operating system, spanning supply planning, manufacturing, production, demand planning, distribution, order fulfillment, and fleet operations. This leader manages through its functional leaders while creating the accountability, operating cadence, and performance standards required to deliver high service levels, consistent quality, and efficient cost structures. While not responsible for cultivation, this leader must also understand cultivation outputs well enough to understand the timing, quality, and characteristics of incoming biomass and translate that supply into effective production and biomass pathway decisions.

Success in this role requires a strong understanding of customer needs, industry dynamics, operational best practices, and hands-on leadership to deliver measurable impact and longterm value across the organization. This position is based in the Sacramento, California area and requires daily onsite presence across facilities.

What You Will Do

• Lead California Operations: Provide strategic and operational leadership across the operations network, including supply planning, manufacturing, production, packaging, warehousing, distribution, fulfillment, and fleet operations.

• Own Supply & Production Planning: Lead integrated demand and supply planning/S&OP in conjunction with capacity planning, inventory strategy, and biomass allocation to align with commercial objectives while minimizing stockouts and aging inventory.

• Drive Operational Accountability: Establish clear KPIs, targets, budgets, and operating rhythms across functional areas; regularly review performance, identify root causes, and drive timely corrective and preventive actions.

• Build Best-in-Class Operations: Develop and maintain standardized operating procedures, efficient workflows and manufacturing layouts, disciplined inventory controls, and scalable operating systems that promote safety, quality, compliance, efficiency, and consistency.

• Optimize Cost, Productivity & Performance: Continuously improve labor, material, freight, inventory, yield, cycle time, equipment utilization, and overall operating costs without compromising service, quality, or compliance.

• Translate Cultivation Supply into Operations: Maintain visibility into cultivation forecasts, harvest timing, biomass quality, and expected volumes to proactively adjust production schedules, processing pathways, capacity, and inventory plans.

• Lead Continuous Improvement & Capital Planning: Identify and execute opportunities in technology, equipment, automation, systems, process improvements, and facility capacity; develop business cases and lead capital planning and implementation to support growth and scalability.

• Manage Suppliers & External Partners: Lead strategic vendor and service-provider relationships, including sourcing, negotiations, performance management, risk mitigation, issue resolution, and business reviews to ensure material availability, service levels, quality, and cost effectiveness.

• Lead Quality, Safety & Compliance: Champion a culture of safety, quality, accountability, and continuous improvement while ensuring compliance with applicable state, local, regulatory, and company quality requirements. Lead root-cause analysis and corrective actions for operational and quality issues.

• Support Product Launches & Operational Transitions: Partner with Commercial, Cultivation, and other stakeholders to translate product and technology roadmaps into operational requirements and successfully execute product launches, new product introduction, process changes, and transitions to scaled production.

• Build Cross-Functional Alignment: Partner closely with Cultivation, Sales, Commercial, Finance, Compliance, R&D, and other stakeholders to align operating plans, resources, and priorities with business objectives and customer commitments.

• Develop High-Performing Teams: Lead, recruit, mentor, and develop functional leaders and operations teams; establish clear ownership and accountability, strengthen leadership capability and succession planning, and foster a data-driven culture of continuous improvement.

• Manage Financial & Operational Reporting: Own operating budgets, forecasts, cost-control initiatives, and performance reporting; provide timely analysis and recommendations to management to support informed business decisions.

Supervisory Responsibilities: This position provides leadership and oversight for the Operations Department and is responsible for organizational structure, performance management, hiring, development, and accountability of Operations team members.

What We Are Looking For

• Bachelor’s degree in Business, Engineering, or a related field.

• 10+ years of progressive leadership experience in multi-facility manufacturing industries.

• Proven ability to lead large, cross-functional teams in a fast-paced environment.

• Hands on ERP experience, critical

• Experience with continuous improvement methodologies and operational excellence programs.

• Excellent communication, leadership, and problem-solving skills.

• Strong financial acumen with experience in budgeting and P&L management.

• Ability to travel ~25% of time - regular monthly travel, required. Compensation Description (annually): The salary range for this position in the selected city is $150,000.00 - $200,000.00 annually. Compensation may vary outside of this range depending on a number of factors, including a candidate’s qualifications, skills, competencies and experience, and location.

Physical Requirements/Workplace Environment

• Requires normal, corrective vision range, the ability to see color and the ability to distinguish letters, numbers and symbols.

• Requires normal hearing range.

• Workplace is a hybrid office setting with frequent travel

The physical demands described here are representative of those that must be met by an employee to successfully perform the essential functions of this position. Reasonable accommodations may be made to enable individuals with disabilities to perform the essential functions of the position.

Why Connected?

Connected is an exciting and innovative workplace with a highly engaged workforce brought together by a shared passion to be the best in the business.  We are on a mission to breed, grow and sell the best cannabis in the world!  This is a super unique opportunity to be part of the start-up stage of the booming cannabis industry.  We are looking for exceptional people to join our team as we transition into the next phase of our business ventures and become a leader in the cannabis space.

jobs.title: Partnerships Lead, Beneficial Deployments
jobs.description:
OpenEvidence is the most widely used medical AI platform in the world.

In just over a year, our usage has grown to >65% of US clinicians via product-led word of mouth adoption. We are a $12B company with a 30 person engineering team from MIT, Harvard, and Stanford. We believe world-changing products come from a small group of exceptional, autonomous builders, organized along focused objectives and empowered to take individual ownership and run fast. We are now bringing OpenEvidence to the clinicians and health workers who need it most: those working in low- and middle-income countries, in low-connectivity and resource-constrained settings, where access to high-quality medical expertise is scarcest and the stakes are highest. If you are a world-class operator in global health who wants to put the best medical AI in the world into the hands of the people delivering care where it is hardest to deliver, we want to talk.



Culture

We believe work is something that should be engaged with at a world-class level. Building 0->1 and scaling 1->1000 are professional sports, and uncompromising excellence is the bar. We believe building things that haven't existed is only possible with end to end ownership. We don't have separate program managers or account teams; you are responsible for landing flagship deployments and demonstrating their impact. Important things are accomplished when an individual decides to accomplish them.



We believe that work should be hard. We believe good work is precise and intentional. Doing something a certain way just because that's how others have done it before guarantees mediocrity. We believe the quality of the product is paramount and the smallest details matter most, including in a rural clinic with intermittent connectivity. At the same time, velocity is essential. The best operators know how to jump right to the hardest part of the problem and build an intuitive experience for health workers. We believe your job is to complete and announce important deployments and demonstrate their impact.



Who are you?

If you are looking to manage a portfolio of partnerships that someone else assembled, this job is not for you. If you are looking to write reports and attend convenings, this job is not for you. If you are looking to lean in and get your hands dirty, bruised, and bloody building a global health program from nothing, personally put OpenEvidence in the hands of health workers across the Global South, and impact hundreds of millions of lives, this job might be for you.



The ideal candidate is a brilliant builder with deep roots in global health. They are smart, ambitious, scrappy, autonomous, precise, motivated, hard-working, and low-ego. They have 10+ years in global health, international development, or related fields, 5+ years managing external partnerships, grantmaking, or multi-stakeholder initiatives, and they have built programs or organizations from scratch. They know the key players at the major NGOs, foundations, and ministries of health, and those people take their calls. Does that sound rare? It is rare, and we would like to find them.



The role

You will be the primary relationship owner for our flagship global health deployments, working with governments, international NGOs, foundations, and innovators strengthening care in low-resource settings. You will grow the partnerships we have, identify and onboard the ones we need, and translate partners' clinical and operational needs into deployment plans that actually work in low-connectivity, low-bandwidth, and offline environments. You will bring on-the-ground insight back to the product, clinical, and research teams and use it to make OpenEvidence best-in-class for global health, including in local languages. You will run structured programs such as accelerators and cohort-based engagements, support funder and ecosystem engagement to sustain the work, and set a research agenda for measuring OpenEvidence's impact on health outcomes in low-resource settings, partnering with external organizations to study efficacy. You will represent OpenEvidence at global health convenings, help shape how the team works as it scales, and spend roughly 25% of your time at partner sites across the Global South.



Skillsets

Specific skillsets are secondary to the builder profile above, but some important spikes for different facets of this work are:



Global health relationships

 - You have deep credibility in the global health ecosystem. You have worked directly with organizations in low- and middle-income countries and have a nuanced understanding of what deployment actually looks like in low-connectivity, low-resource environments.

 - You may have language skills relevant to Sub-Saharan Africa, or Latin America, or a background in clinical or public health settings.

Technical fluency

 - You can engage credibly on AI concepts, understand what LLMs can and cannot do, and partner effectively with engineers and scientists. You might come from a healthtech company, an AI organization, or a product-adjacent role.

Programs and funders

 - You have built and run structured programs from scratch, likely at a startup or in a founding role, and you have worked with philanthropic foundations on global health initiatives.

 - You are comfortable managing a high volume of partnerships and opportunities and ruthless about prioritizing among them.

Impact and evidence

 - You have an analytical mindset and use data to inform strategy and measure impact. Evaluation and quantitative proof are tools you constantly seek to deploy.

 - You are familiar with global health research and evidence-based interventions, and you want to prove, not assert, that OpenEvidence improves outcomes.



We work in-person in Miami and SF, and this role travels extensively (~25%) to partner sites across the Global South. We believe in creating an environment that optimizes for focus and productivity, including providing meals, transport, and anything else you need to move quickly.

jobs.title: Implementation Consultant II, Construction
jobs.description:
Built's Mission: Connect and simplify doing business in real estate.

Built is the AI-powered platform transforming the way real estate is financed, developed, and managed. Purpose-built for real estate and construction, Built began by fixing construction draw management for lenders and has grown into a comprehensive operating system addressing some of the industry’s most complex challenges. Today, Built is a partner to more than 350 lenders, over 80,000 borrowers and owners, and thousands of contractors, powering 86,000 active projects valued at more than $300 billion. Learn more at getbuilt.com.
__________________________

Built Technologies is transforming how capital moves through construction and real estate finance - one of the largest, most complex sectors in the economy. Our platform connects lenders, including many of the top U.S. banks, with the owners, developers, and general contractors they finance. When a draw is approved, a builder can pay subcontractors. When a compliance document clears, a project moves forward. The work we do here is not abstract; it has a direct and material impact on how capital flows and how real estate gets built.

Our Implementations team delivers the platform experiences that determine whether a lender adopts Built as their operational backbone or walks away. As an Implementation Consultant II, you will manage a strategic portfolio of complex client implementations with growing independence; owning end-to-end delivery for enterprise-scale lending clients and beginning to contribute to how the broader team operates. You bring a track record of successful go-lives, strong client relationships, and the judgment to navigate novel challenges without constant direction. This role supports owners, developers, and general contractors and is especially well suited to someone who brings construction context plus the ability to learn and deliver software.

Our Guiding Principles

• Be Bold. We pursue the biggest problems in our industry, challenge assumptions others take for granted, and take calculated risks to get there. We don't hide behind consensus or committees. Playing it safe is just failing slowly.

• Help Customers Win. We learn our customers' businesses deeply — how they think, how they deploy capital, what keeps them up at night. We treat their capital like our own. We ship leverage, not features. And we measure ourselves by customer results, not our intentions.

• Move with Urgency & Purpose. We bias toward delivery over perfection, remove friction from our own paths, and communicate in real time. Momentum compounds — and we build it every day.

• Own the Outcome. We own outcomes, not just tasks. We hold a high Say:Do ratio and take responsibility from idea through impact. When something breaks, we fix it — we don't wait to be asked.

• Never Satisfied. We raise the bar continuously. We stay curious, hold exacting standards, debate hard, and hold our opinions loosely when the evidence shifts. Excellence is a habit, not an event.

What You'll Do

• Lead complex implementations for owner, developer, and general contractor clients - managing project scope, risk, and timeline with meaningful autonomy and clear accountability for outcomes.

• Conduct discovery and planning sessions with client stakeholders, translating strategic business goals and workflows into actionable implementation roadmaps.

• Manage escalations and navigate organizational dynamics on the client side, driving timely resolution of high-impact issues with composure and authority.

• Identify process improvements and standardization opportunities across your implementation portfolio — document repeatable solutions and share them with the broader team.

• Contribute to cross-functional initiatives with Sales, Product, and Engineering to improve implementation efficiency, reduce time-to-value, and strengthen client outcomes.

• Track and communicate implementation metrics, insights, and lessons learned to leadership and the broader team; use data to surface patterns and drive improvement.

• Leverage AI tools to accelerate project planning, client communication, and risk identification across your portfolio.

What You'll Bring

• 2-4 years of experience in SaaS implementation, professional services, or enterprise project delivery, ideally in construction technology, financial services, fintech, or a complex B2B software environment.

• Construction industry experience is strongly preferred. You have worked for or closely with an owner, developer, general contractor, subcontractor, or construction technology company, and understand the operational realities of running projects.

• A proven ability to deliver concurrent client implementations on time and to a high standard, with examples of measurable client outcomes you drove.

• Strong client communication and relationship management skills; you navigate senior stakeholders, handle difficult conversations with confidence, and build trust through consistent follow-through.

• A track record of identifying process improvements that made implementations faster, more consistent, or more successful for clients.

• Working knowledge of construction project and financial workflows, such as project set-up, project financials, payables, lien waivers, project controls, or subcontractor/vendor coordination. You can use that context to help a customer translate how they work today into a practical workflow in Built.

• Some experience with implementation methodologies (Agile, Waterfall, or hybrid approaches) and comfort adapting your approach to the client's environment.

• Comfort with project management tools, CRM systems, and analytics platforms; ability to learn new tools quickly and apply them effectively.

What Success Looks Like at Six Months

• Your implementation portfolio is delivering consistently — projects are on schedule, clients are satisfied, and go-lives are producing measurable adoption outcomes.

• You've successfully navigated at least one high-complexity or high-risk implementation to a successful go-live, demonstrating sound judgment under pressure.

• You've contributed at least one process improvement or documented playbook that has been adopted by the broader implementations team.

• Cross-functional partners in Sales, Product, and Engineering consistently seek your input when complex client situations arise, trusting your judgment and domain expertise.

AI & Technology Expectations

• Leverage AI tools to enhance the productivity, quality, and speed of your work. • Use AI to support drafting, analysis, summarization, and problem-solving across your role. • Identify opportunities to streamline workflows and reduce manual effort through automation and AI.

• Apply AI to sharpen decision-making and strengthen strategic insights.

• Share effective AI use cases and best practices with your team.

Built’s salary range for this position is $90,000 - 115,000 USD per year. The pay range is designed to accommodate upward mobility in the role, therefore it encompasses the full span of proficiency levels for this role and we believe that the midpoint of the range is competitive in the market. Salary is just one component of Built's total compensation package for employees; your total rewards package at Built will include equity, market-current medical, dental and vision coverage, an unlimited PTO policy, and other benefits.

__________________________

Travel Requirement: Employees who are not based in the Nashville area are required to travel to our Nashville office at least twice per year for company gatherings, such as Connect Week. Additional travel to Nashville may be required based on your role and business needs.

Perks:

• The rare opportunity to radically disrupt a $1.5T industry

• Competitive benefits including: uncapped vacation [US ONLY], medical, dental & vision insurance

• Robust compensation package, including equity in the form of stock options

• Learning Grant program to support ongoing professional development

🧬 What We're Looking For

• 5+ years of professional copywriting experience, ideally including direct-response, performance marketing, or e-commerce work.

• A portfolio or writing samples that show range - punchy hooks as well as longer-form marketing copy.

• Comfort writing to a brief, incorporating feedback quickly, and adjusting tone for different brands and audiences.

• Based in the United States, able to work U.S. business hours with your team.

➕ Nice To Have

• Experience writing specifically for Meta, TikTok, or YouTube ad formats.

• Familiarity with direct-response frameworks (e.g., PAS, AIDA) or performance-marketing terminology (CPA, ROAS, hook rate).

• Background in e-commerce, DTC, or subscription-based brands.

💡 Work at the intersection of data and creativity — your ideas have measurable impact

🎬 Get exposure to the largest advertisers on Meta and TikTok across diverse verticals

🚀 Grow fast in a high-performance environment with mentorship from senior strategists

🤝 Collaborate daily with creative, production, and data teams

jobs.title: Director of Implementation
jobs.description:
ABOUT DOCTRONIC


Doctronic is the #1 AI doctor. Our AI is free, anonymous and HIPAA-compliant, and it has delivered over 30 million consults to date. In December 2025 we became the first and only AI legally authorized to practice medicine, renewing prescriptions autonomously under Utah's AI Learning Lab, and the first AI ever granted medical malpractice insurance. We are live in all 50 states and DC with AI and human physicians available 24/7, and we have raised $65M through our Series B from Abstract, Lightspeed, Union Square Ventures and others.

We are now building the enterprise organization that takes this to health plans, health systems and the wider healthcare ecosystem. This role owns everything that happens after a partner signs.



THE ROLE

Every signed partnership goes live on time, at quality, without engineering heroics. That is the whole mandate.

We have live partners today and more in build, and we have learned the hard way that launch quality currently depends too much on who happens to be assigned. You will fix that: build the delivery pods, build the repeatable launch process, and own the launch date. Your primary metric is on-time launch rate, with a target of moving signature to go-live under 60 days.

You will report to the Chief Business Officer and lead a team of deployment strategists and solutions engineers, growing to three pods. You will also be the escalation path for partners, which today defaults to engineering and should not.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own the launch of every enterprise partnership from signature to go-live, across co-branded deployments, embedded chat and API integrations

 - Build and lead delivery pods, each pairing a deployment strategist who owns the plan and the partner relationship with one to two solutions engineers

 - Own the requirements document and hold the line on scope. If a partner asks for something new, it goes to the deal desk and product, not into the build

 - Own the technical service level agreement and the delivery commitments we make in every statement of work, including before signature

 - Stand up the launch playbook: internal kickoff at 80% closed, external kickoff, build, QA, clinical readiness, go-live, and the 30-day retro

 - Run the handoff from sales, and make sure nobody walks into a partner kickoff without having read the statement of work

 - Partner with our Enterprise Product Lead on the bespoke versus platform call, and drive the share of partner requirements we can meet with existing product upward every quarter

 - Own the reuse verdict after each launch: template it, productize it, or retire it

 - Be the escalation path, so that engineering can build instead of firefight
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 8+ years in implementation, professional services, technical program management or solutions delivery, including 3+ years managing people

 - Has delivered technical integrations into regulated enterprises: health systems, payers, pharmacy, or financial services

 - Technically fluent. APIs, webhooks, SSO, and healthcare data standards such as FHIR. You can hold your own with engineers and be useful in the conversation

 - Has told a customer no and kept the relationship. This is the single most important thing we are screening for

 - Has built process where none existed, rather than administered process someone else designed

 - Writes clearly and runs a meeting well. Most of the failure modes in this job are communication failures

 - Based in New York City or willing to relocate. This is a hybrid role
   


NICE TO HAVE

 - FHIR R4, HL7, or direct Epic or Cerner integration experience

 - Has run a pod, squad or forward-deployed engineering model

 - Telehealth or clinical workflow delivery experience

 - Experience introducing self-service tooling or a partner portal to reduce manual onboarding

 - Has owned a technical SLA and the support tiering behind it
   


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Base salary range: $225-$250k + equity

 - Health reimbursement allowance, support for well-being, and flexible time off

jobs.title: Manager, Electrode Process Engineering, Operations
jobs.description:
Are you ready to build America’s energy future? Form Energy is an American manufacturing and energy technology company. We’re revolutionizing energy storage with cost-effective, multi-day technology designed to keep the electric grid secure and reliable, even during extended periods of stress. By strengthening the electric system and reimagining what’s possible, we’re giving clean energy a whole new form! 



In recent years, Form Energy has earned a number of accolades, including being named by TIME as a “Best Invention”, MIT Technology Review as a “Top Climate Tech Company To Watch”, and Fast Company as “One of the Next Big Things In Tech”. We are making rapid progress on our mission of delivering energy storage for a better world, and our team is growing just as rapidly to meet demand. We have signed contracts with leading electric utilities across the United States and production of our iron-air batteries is underway at our first high-volume manufacturing facility in West Virginia. 



Working for Form Energy is more than just a job, it’s a chance to be part of something extraordinary. And now - right as we significantly scale up battery manufacturing -  might be the most exciting moment in the company’s history to join. We are assembling a team of highly talented and driven individuals across the country. Driven by our core values of humanity, excellence, and creativity, our team is determined to deliver on our mission and transform the energy landscape for the better.



Feeling energized to make a meaningful impact on the world? Then keep reading - you’ve come to the right place.




ROLE DESCRIPTION

Form Energy is hiring a Process Engineering Manager to oversee our Electrode Manufacturing Operations. In this role, you will lead a team of process engineers, equipment engineers, and technicians responsible for the performance, reliability, and efficiency of our electrode production lines — spanning powder handling, mixing, and roll-to-roll tape formation processes. You'll bring strong technical judgment grounded in material science, along with a data-driven approach, to guide your team in diagnosing process issues, prioritizing improvement projects, and implementing robust, high-impact solutions on the floor. You will own staffing, coaching, and performance management for your team, while partnering with cross-functional engineering leaders to translate process and materials insights into meaningful, lasting manufacturing improvements. This is a unique opportunity to leverage your process engineering background, materials expertise, and leadership experience to build a world-class, fully automated electrode production process.


Relocation assistance is available. 




WHAT YOU'LL DO:

 - Own the section's operating results across powder handling, mixing, and roll-to-roll tape formation, holding your team accountable for line cadence, downtime, and overall throughput

 - Manage and develop a small, mostly-engineer team of process engineers, equipment engineers, and technicians, including staffing, coaching, and performance decisions

 - Establish and track section-level metrics (OEE, yield, cycle time) and direct resourcing toward the highest-impact bottlenecks across each process step

 - Set methods and standards for evaluating and vetting floor-level solutions, ensuring fixes across the powder-to-tape process are safe, robust, and grounded in sound material science before scale-up

 - Represent the section in cross-functional planning with peer engineering and manufacturing teams, resolving constraints that affect quality and throughput company-wide

 - Build and prioritize a continuous improvement roadmap for the section, balancing waste reduction, ergonomics, and process reliability against production demands




WHAT YOU'LL BRING:

 - Bachelor's degree in Materials Science, Chemical, Mechanical, or Manufacturing Engineering, or related field

 - 7+ years in manufacturing/production operations, including team management experience

 - Strong material science foundation — able to connect powder properties and tape mechanics to process outcomes

 - Proven track record hiring, developing, and managing process/equipment engineers or technicians

 - Deep familiarity with manufacturing metrics (OEE, downtime) and a root-cause approach to problem-solving

 - Working knowledge of roll-to-roll processes — powder transformation, mixing, web handling

 - Strong influencing skills and experience representing your team's priorities to peer managers and engineering leadership

 - Pragmatic, curious, and comfortable with ambiguity as the organization scales
   




WHERE YOU'LL WORK:


This role is based at Form Factory 1 in Weirton, WV—an easy commute from the city of Pittsburgh, PA. This 550,000-square-foot facility is our hub for high-volume battery production and a leader in the new era of American energy manufacturing. Relocation assistance is available.



#LI-Onsite

#LI-LN1





Humanity is a cornerstone of Form Energy’s culture, and we make sure our compensation and benefits reflect that. Form Energy offers competitive salaries, stock options, and a holistic benefits package to ensure all employees have what they need to thrive while working here. 



When it comes to you and your family’s health, we cover 100% of medical, dental, and vision premiums for full-time employees - and 80% of healthcare premiums for dependents. This starts from day one. We also offer at least 12 weeks of paid leave for new parents (up to 20 weeks for birthing parents), and generous vacation policies to give employees time to recharge when needed. 



To build America’s energy future, we need everyone at the table. We are proud to be an equal opportunity employer, and encourage candidates from all backgrounds to apply to our open jobs.

Position Summary

The Data and Evaluation Associate's primary responsibilities are to: 1) prepare regular reports on key programs to for program leaders and administrators; 2) support the design of rigorous mixed methods program and agency evaluations (integrating qualitative and quantitative data); 3) help design and administer program evaluation tools that measure program compliance and quality; 4) monitor programs' quality and compliance; 5) analyze administrative, compliance, and quality data; 6) design, test, and administer stakeholder surveys. The Associate will divide their time equally between PMT. where they will be supervised by a Data and Evaluation Manager, and the Mayor's Office of Education (MOE), where they will work on-site with program staff.

Essential Functions

1) Support the design and implementation of research and evaluation projects that advance program and system performance improvements for Adult Education, Extended Day Extended Year and other MOE programs.

2) Clean, manage, and integrate data from key system sources to produce short and long-term outcome analyses. Key data sources include but are not limited to case file reviews, program narratives, program observations, surveys, and administrative data on enrollment, attendance, invoicing, activities and outcomes.

3) Prepare and submit quarterly MOE data reports for internal and public audiences.

4) Generate graphs, tables, and other data visuals.

5) Assist in survey design, administration, and analysis.

6) Automate regular data reporting of administrative, compliance, and quality data.

7) Monitor contract compliance by coding and maintaining provider-specific automated monthly reports.

a. Monitor and support the collection Of program evaluation data using CQI tools across the AEPHL network of adult education providers.

b. Clean, analyze, and disseminate provider-level CQI data for AEPHL network partners.

c. Analyze CQ and evaluation data in aggregate to communicate trends in program improvement to all MOE and AEPHL stakeholders.

12) Advise teammates on measurement and evaluation processes, including formulating research questions, planning the scope of evaluation, and developing feedback cycles between data collection and data analysis.

13) Develop written reports and presentations for a variety of audiences using clear, concise language.

Northpoint Recovery Holdings, LLC began 2009 as Ashwood Outpatient and officially launched the Northpoint platform in 2015. Now celebrating 10 years of growth in 2025, Northpoint is a leading behavioral healthcare provider offering evidence-based treatment for adults with substance use and co-occurring disorders through the Northpoint Recovery brand, and mental health treatment for adolescents through Imagine by Northpoint. Operating under an in-network, commercial insurance model, Northpoint has grown exclusively through de novo expansion—from two facilities to seventeen across the Western U.S.—with more planned in both existing and new markets. • Consultation to physicians and providers regarding any ongoing medical care, maintenance and disease prevention

jobs.title: Vertical Sales Lead, Health Plans (Payer)
jobs.description:
ABOUT DOCTRONIC

Doctronic is the #1 AI doctor. Our AI is free, anonymous and HIPAA-compliant, and it has delivered over 30 million consults to date. In December 2025 we became the first and only AI legally authorized to practice medicine, renewing prescriptions autonomously under Utah's AI Learning Lab, and the first AI ever granted medical malpractice insurance. We are live in all 50 states and DC with AI and human physicians available 24/7, and we have raised $65M through our Series B from Abstract, Lightspeed, Union Square Ventures and others.

We are now building the enterprise organization that takes this to health plans, health systems and the wider healthcare ecosystem. This is one of the first senior sales hires on that team.



THE ROLE

You will own the health plan vertical end to end: the pipeline, the relationships, the narrative, and the number. Regional and national commercial payers, Medicare Advantage plans, Medicaid managed care organizations, and third-party administrators.

This is a fulltime role at a company where the product is genuinely new, so you will spend as much time teaching the market what autonomous clinical AI can do as you will running a process. You will report to the Chief Business Officer and work alongside our Chief Medical Officer, who carries the clinical credibility that opens these rooms.



WHAT YOU'LL DO

 - Own pipeline generation and closed contract value for the health plan vertical, with a target of at least four opportunities in contracting or later at any time

 - Build the payer narrative and buyer persona map: total cost of care, access and network adequacy, member engagement, quality measures, and performance in value-based arrangements

 - Run the full cycle, sourcing with business development and marketing, scoping the integration with solutions engineering, and closing with the deal desk

 - Navigate payer procurement and compliance, including security review, diligence questionnaires, corporate practice of medicine considerations, and BAA and DUA negotiation

 - Work with our Chief Medical Officer and research team to turn clinical evidence into payer-ready economic packages

 - Partner with implementation before signature so that what you sell is what we can deliver, on the timeline you committed to

 - Feed vertical requirements into the enterprise product roadmap, and push back on one-off builds that will not repeat

 - Grow accounts after launch alongside customer success, because expansion inside a plan matters more to us than net-new logos
   


WHAT WE'RE LOOKING FOR

 - 10+ years selling into health plans, including multi-year enterprise contracts you personally closed and carried a number against

 - Verifiable relationships with payer economic buyers: chief medical officers, VPs of clinical operations and network, and digital health or innovation leaders

 - Fluency in payer economics and the vocabulary that goes with it: PMPM, risk adjustment, medical loss ratio, capitation, shared savings and value-based contracting

 - A track record of selling clinical credibility rather than features, and the judgment to know which evidence a given buyer actually needs

 - Comfort selling a product that is still moving, in a category that regulators are still defining

 - Willingness to travel heavily. Our enterprise buyers do not buy over video alone

 - Based in New York City or willing to relocate. This is a hybrid role
   


NICE TO HAVE

 - Sold AI, digital health or virtual care into payers specifically

 - Worked inside a health plan, on the buying side of a deal like this one

 - Familiarity with CMS models and care management programs such as ACCESS, APCM, CCM and TCM

 - Experience with co-branded or digital front door deployments inside a plan's member experience

 - Early-stage experience, ideally as one of the first sellers in a vertical
   


COMPENSATION & BENEFITS

 - Base salary range: $225-$275k + commission of up to 50% of base

 - Meaningful equity

 - Health reimbursement allowance, support for well-being, and flexible time off

jobs.title: Clinical Program Director: School-Based K-12
jobs.description:
CLINICAL PROGRAM DIRECTOR

Location

NuView Academy, Piscataway NJ

Setting

State-run therapeutic day school: a self-contained program for K-12 students with the highest level of emotional, behavioral, and mental health needs

Schedule

Full-time, 12-month schedule (academic/clinical calendar runs through summer, with school breaks off plus two weeks in August). Monday–Friday, primarily daytime, with one evening per week for coverage and a monthly evening parent support group. No weekends.

Reports To

Clinical Regional Director

Salary Range

$90,000–$95,000, commensurate with experience and licensure

About the Role

Effective School Solutions (ESS) is a well-established, rapidly growing organization changing the nature of in-school mental health services for K-12 students.

The Clinical Program Director leads the clinical and operational success of ESS's program at NuView Academy, supporting K-12 students with the highest level of need — many of whom are stepping down from hospitalization or residential care, or could not be safely maintained in a traditional public school. This is a high-responsibility, high-impact role: you'll provide leadership to clinical staff, own program operations, and serve as the primary point of contact between ESS and school leadership, all while making sure some of the highest-need students in the state get the intensive care they need to stabilize and move forward.

This role is built for a seasoned, independently licensed clinician who is ready to lead at a program level. It's a fast-paced environment where priorities shift quickly, so comfort anticipating needs before they're voiced and making sound decisions with incomplete information goes a long way. You bring deep clinical expertise with acute, high-need student populations, real experience managing and developing clinical leaders and teams, and the relationship-building skills to earn trust with school and state education leadership alike. In return, you'll get a structured, well-resourced program to run, a team of experienced clinical and educational leaders behind you, and the kind of ownership that comes with building something that works, plus extensive training in ESS protocols, systems, and service models as you get started.

What You'll Do

Clinical Leadership

• Provide weekly individual clinical supervision (~9 hours/week) to Clinicians and Mental Health Technicians, including consultation and oversight for individual, group, and family interventions.

• Lead weekly consultation meetings on treatment planning, progress monitoring, and documentation compliance.

• Represent ESS in IEP meetings, manifestation determinations, disciplinary hearings, and re-entry planning following hospitalization or disciplinary action.

• Coordinate care across families, school staff, psychiatrists, and community providers so students move smoothly across the full continuum of care.

• Collaborate directly with the psychiatrist on medication management — appointment setting, confirmation, and follow-through with families and the school nurse — acting as the bridge between psychiatry and the school.

• Build strong multidisciplinary partnerships that support students' academic, behavioral, and emotional success.

• Lead family engagement efforts, including a monthly in-person parent support group, parent meetings, and educational programming.

• Serve as the program's go-to expert for managing crises and high-risk student situations and be available by phone to support staff providing after-hours family therapy.

Program & Operational Leadership

• Own day-to-day program operations and people management for the clinical team — staffing, scheduling, adherence to ESS standards, performance feedback, annual reviews, and corrective action, in partnership with the Clinical Regional Director and HR.

• Partner with ESS's Regional Recruiting Manager on interviewing and hiring clinical staff.

• Serve as the primary point of contact with school and district leadership on program needs, outcomes, and student support, and report program progress to district and ESS leadership.

• Identify potential clinical, relationship, or staffing issues early, and resolve them independently and effectively.

• Coordinate with school leaders on tours, referrals, and assessment scheduling for prospective students and families.

• Step in to cover clinical coverage gaps when needed.

• Ensure clinical documentation is accurate, timely, and compliant with ESS, ethical, and regulatory standards.

• Track and analyze program data (attendance, behavior, academics, utilization) and turn it into action plans that close performance gaps.

• Represent ESS professionally across the district, traveling as needed to support your team.

What You Bring

Required

• Master's degree in Social Work, Counseling, Marriage and Family Therapy, or a related mental health field.

• Active, independent clinical license (LCSW, LPC, LMFT) in NJ.

• Certification to provide clinical supervision.

• 6–8 years providing clinical services to children and adolescents with significant behavioral, emotional, or mental health challenges.

• 3–5 years of supervisory or leadership experience in a clinical setting.

• Proven ability to build trust and strong working relationships with school administrators, district leaders, families, and community partners.

• Strong leadership, communication, organizational, and project management skills, with a solution-focused approach to problem solving.

• Proficiency with Microsoft Office and electronic documentation/EHR systems.

Preferred

• Prior experience in a school-based mental health program.

• Experience supervising multidisciplinary teams.

• Comfort using data to drive clinical and operational decisions.

Compensation & Benefits

• Salary Range: $90,000–$95,000, based on experience and licensure.

• Health, dental, and vision coverage.

• 401K plan with employer match.

• Company-paid life insurance and disability coverage.

• PTO and paid holidays.

• Access to CEUs and professional development.

• Employee Assistance Program (EAP), plus access to discount programs for entertainment/travel and a childcare network.

Why Join Effective School Solutions?

• Be part of a mission-driven organization addressing the growing mental health needs of children and adolescents.

• Work alongside experienced clinical and educational leaders dedicated to improving student outcomes.

• Step into a real leadership track: this role is a launchpad toward regional and multi-site clinical leadership opportunities.

• Contribute your expertise to an organization that values clinician voice, collaboration, and continuous improvement.

Equal Opportunity Employer

ESS is an Equal Opportunity Employer and does not discriminate against any employee or applicant for employment on the basis of race, color, sex, age, national origin, religion, sexual orientation, gender identity and/or expression, status as a veteran, and basis of disability or any other federal, state or local protected class.

jobs.title: Therapeutic Account Manager, Liver - Dallas
jobs.description:
MISSION

Mirum Pharmaceuticals is a biopharmaceutical company dedicated to transforming the treatment of rare diseases. We are passionate about advancing scientific discoveries to become important medicines for rare disease patients. We are collaborative, creative, and experienced professionals and we’re looking to augment our team with other individuals who embody our values: care, be real, get it done, and have fun, seriously.

POSITION SUMMARY

The Therapeutic Account Manager (TAM) is responsible for delivering strong, sustainable business performance and meaningful patient impact across an assigned territory. The TAM develops deep clinical and account expertise in rare cholestatic liver diseases and Mirum's Liver portfolio; identifies and prioritizes high-opportunity customers, accounts, and referral networks; and executes customized account plans that advance disease awareness, appropriate patient identification, treatment consideration, initiation, and persistence in accordance with approved indications and promotional practices.

The ideal TAM is not a transactional seller. This individual is a clinically credible, insight-led partner who engages healthcare professionals as a peer, asks thoughtful questions, constructively challenges clinical inertia, and influences change across complex accounts. The TAM works closely with the Regional Business Director and cross-functional partners to connect customer needs, patient journeys, referral pathways, access dynamics, and business opportunities while demonstrating curiosity, high emotional intelligence, resilience, ownership, and consistent follow-through.

JOB FUNCTIONS/RESPONSIBILITIES

Territory Strategy & Business Performance

• Develop and execute a focused territory business plan aligned with national, zone, and regional priorities, with clear objectives, customer priorities, resource allocation, and measures of success.

• Use performance data, customer insights, market intelligence, access dynamics, and competitive trends to identify opportunities, anticipate barriers, and make timely adjustments to territory strategy and execution.

• Delivers territory business objectives through disciplined prioritization, high-quality customer engagement, effective resource stewardship, and accountability for both behaviors and results.

• Maintain accurate and timely customer records, forecasts, expense reporting, required administrative documentation, and business updates in accordance with company expectations.

Strategic Account Management & Network Development

• Identify, prioritize, and develop high-opportunity accounts, health systems, centers of excellence, and referral networks across pediatric and adult hepatology and gastroenterology.

• Create and execute customized account plans that reflect the local patient journey, key stakeholders, clinical decision-making, referral patterns, access considerations, customer needs, and competitive realities.

• Build trusted relationships with physicians, advanced practice providers, nurses, pharmacists, office staff, and other members of the care team by delivering relevant value and consistent follow-through.

• Map influence and decision-making within complex accounts, establish clear objectives for each engagement, and secure appropriate next steps that advance the account strategy.

• Coordinate compliant account actions across Mirum field partners, clarify ownership, and maintain momentum against agreed priorities and customer needs.

Clinical Aptitude & Customer Engagement

• Develop and maintain deep knowledge of rare cholestatic liver disease, diagnostic pathways, mechanisms of action, clinical data, product profiles, approved uses, safety information, patient support pathways, access and reimbursement, and the evolving competitive landscape.

• Communicate complex scientific and clinical information clearly, accurately, and credibly, tailoring the discussion to the knowledge, needs, and priorities of each healthcare professional and account.

• Engage healthcare professionals as a clinically credible peer by asking insightful questions, listening actively, uncovering unmet needs, and connecting relevant evidence and resources to the customer's practice.

• Execute approved promotional programs, resources, and customer engagements with consistency, clinical relevance, sound judgment, and full adherence to company policies and regulatory requirements.

Influence & Impact

• Help customers recognize gaps in disease awareness, patient identification, referral, treatment consideration, and ongoing support by reframing issues and connecting insights across the patient journey.

• Use high emotional intelligence, curiosity, credibility, and thoughtful questioning to build trust with skeptical, change-resistant, or highly experienced healthcare professionals.

• Influence multiple stakeholders without authority, navigate resistance constructively, and balance persistence with judgment, empathy, and respect for customer boundaries

Customer, Patient & Caregiver Impact

• Keep patients and caregivers at the center of territory and account decisions, with a clear understanding of the journey from disease recognition and diagnosis through treatment initiation and persistence.

• Support a customer experience grounded in trust, empathy, responsiveness, urgency, and reliable follow-through with healthcare professionals and care teams.

• Collaborate compliantly with Market Access and Patient Services partners to help care teams understand available resources and navigate appropriate barriers in the patient journey.

• Identify recurring customer, access, and patient-support barriers; elevate them objectively and promptly; and partner with the appropriate internal teams to improve execution and support.

Cross-Functional Collaboration & Field Insights

• Build productive partnerships with Medical Affairs, Market Access, Patient Services, Marketing, Commercial Training and Effectiveness, Operations, Analytics, and Advocacy.

• Work seamlessly across field roles to coordinate account strategy, align priorities, clarify responsibilities, and ensure consistent follow-through while respecting functional boundaries.

• Capture and communicate timely, objective, and actionable field insights that can inform strategy, messaging, training, resource development, customer experience, and execution priorities.

• Contribute actively to business reviews, training programs, team meetings, launch readiness, and cross-functional initiatives; share best practices and support the success of the broader organization.

Entrepreneurial Drive, Resilience & Culture

• Operate with a high degree of ownership, self-motivation, resourcefulness, and initiative in an unstructured, rapidly evolving rare disease environment.

• Create appropriate engagement opportunities in underdeveloped accounts and markets, test new approaches, learn quickly, and translate insights into action.

• Maintain sustained drive, discipline, and performance through pressure, uncertainty, obstacles, delays, and discouragement; recover quickly and remain focused on long-term goals.

• Demonstrate curiosity, coachability, and a commitment to continuous learning; actively seek feedback and apply coaching to strengthen clinical, strategic, and selling capabilities.

• Model Mirum's values and the highest standards of ethical conduct, compliance, transparency, inclusion, and respect in every internal and external interaction.

QUALIFICATIONS

Education/Experience:

• Bachelor's degree required; advanced degree preferred.

• 5+ years of progressive sales experience in the pharmaceutical or biotechnology industry.

• Demonstrated track record of consistently delivering business results in a complex specialty, rare disease, orphan drug, or high-science market.

• Rare disease experience is highly preferred; experience in hepatology, gastroenterology, pediatric specialty care, or another complex specialty market is highly desirable.

• Strong clinical aptitude and demonstrated ability to learn, retain, and communicate complex disease-state, diagnostic, mechanism-of-action, clinical-data, and product information.

• Experience with account-based selling across health systems, centers of excellence, multidisciplinary care teams, referral networks, and influential healthcare professionals.

• Demonstrated ability to use insight-led or challenger-style selling to constructively challenge the status quo, influence behavior, and advance customer decision-making.

• Working knowledge of access and reimbursement dynamics, patient support pathways, and the role of patient services in rare disease markets.

• Strong business acumen and ability to interpret performance data, identify insights, develop territory and account strategies, and translate plans into consistent field execution.

• Exceptional interpersonal skills, emotional intelligence, communication, presentation, judgment, and ability to build trust with diverse and highly sophisticated customers.

• Proven self-motivation, resourcefulness, resilience, organization, and ability to prioritize and perform independently in a fast-moving, ambiguous environment.

• Demonstrated success partnering cross-functionally with Medical Affairs, Market Access, Patient Services, Marketing, Commercial Training and Effectiveness, Operations, and Analytics.

• Commitment to ethical conduct, compliance, and approved promotional practices, with sound judgment in complex customer and patient-related situations.

• Valid driver's license and ability to travel up to 70%, including frequent overnight travel and occasional weekend commitments.

#LI-REMOTE

Mirum Pharmaceuticals is committed to Equal Employment Opportunity (EEO) and to compliance with all Federal, State and Local laws that prohibit employment discrimination on the basis of race, age, national origin, ethnicity, religion, gender, gender identity, pregnancy, marital status, sexual orientation, citizenship, genetic disposition or characteristics, disability, veteran’s status or any other classification protected by applicable State/Federal/Local laws.

Mirum Pharmaceuticals provides reasonable accommodation for qualified individuals with disabilities and disabled veterans in job application procedures.
